Cnoc dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,587

Founded 4 am Màrt 1079 DE by carters of Caol fhiadhaich. Known for carters' stop on the south-west road.

A small town on a straight hill road between Caol fhiadhaich and the great mill-town of Muileann bheag. It follows the order of the Stone and is a stop for carters.

Muileann bheag

fort · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 13,749

Founded 31 an Cèitean 1256 DE by wardens of the panther roads. Known for citadel north of the panther roads.

Muileann bheag is a fort with a citadel north of Baile dhomhain, whose fields the panthers of Imrich nam Pantar cross. It is not the Muileann bheag of the northern lighthouse. Travellers stop at Am Buabhall Fortanach nearby, and the first fleet lies at Àth gharbh a short way west.

Siorrachd Caol gharbh

Caol chrom

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,192

Founded 13 an Dùbhlachd 1236 DE by the garrison of the bent strait. Known for fortified bent strait.

Caol chrom is a fortified harbour on a bent strait of the north-east, walled and given a citadel in the long quiet centuries. It is a city by rank but small in people, and its garrison has always outnumbered its fishermen. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith. Its few townsmen boil soap and blow glass for the hill towns. Its headmen and Caol gharbh's meet at Coinneachadh na h-Amhaich, the stone on the neck of land between the two harbours, to settle the dues of the strait.

  • 7 an Gearran 1977 DE — The north-eastern harbours

Caol gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 26,717

Founded 5 am Màrt 2276 BDE by Ròdaich seafarers of the rough strait. Known for boatyards on the rough strait.

Caol gharbh is a walled harbour on the rough strait and the seat of its province, a village in name but a town of twenty-seven thousand in fact. Its boatyards take oak from Doire chaol and build the heavy boats the strait demands. Its quarrel with Seann Bhrenn next door is as old as the rolls. Its headmen and Caol chrom's meet at Coinneachadh na h-Amhaich, the stone on the neck of land between the two harbours, to settle the dues of the strait.

  • 8 an t-Ògmhios 1130 DE — Caol gharbh takes the salt
  • 10 an t-Samhain 1695 DE — Caol gharbh loses the salt
  • 11 an Gearran 1833 DE — Caol gharbh bypassed

Doire chaol

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,925

Founded 22 an Lùnastal 723 DE by woodwards for Caol gharbh's yards. Known for oak for Caol gharbh's boatyards.

A village in a narrow oakwood that has sent timber to the boatyards of Caol gharbh since the yards were opened. It has always been small and has always been owed money by the yards. Its families also hunt the oakwood, and their venison goes down to Caol gharbh with the timber. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Siorrachd Caol ìseal

Baile shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,859

Founded 13 an Dùbhlachd 2272 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the northern shore. Known for old quay of the northern shore.

Baile shean is an old quay on the northern shore and the port of its province. The inn An Taigh-seinnse Reòta lies inland on the road south, and its pickled spinach goes out through the quay. It is one of several places named Baile shean.

Caol ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 16,600

Founded 21 am Màrt 1549 BDE by salt-makers of the northern coast. Known for salt pans of the low strait.

Caol ìseal is a harbour town on a low strait of the north coast and the seat of its province. Its salt pans have supplied the northern fisheries since the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. Bog-iron dug behind the pans feeds its forges, which cast field-guns for the regiments.

  • 31 an Cèitean 1330 DE — The Caol ìseal fishers go east
  • 2 an Gearran 1915 DE — Powder landed at Caol ìseal

Cnoc bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,395

Founded 21 am Màrt 5 BDE by fishers of Caol ìseal. Known for white-hill kelp and herring.

Cnoc bhàn grew as an overflow of the harbour at Caol ìseal, a white hill with a landing at its foot. Its boats work the kelp beds and the herring of the northern shore. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and has never needed walls.

Cnoc uaine

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,458

Founded 17 an t-Ògmhios 1266 DE by the garrison of the north-coast road. Known for hill fort over the north-coast road.

Cnoc uaine of Caol ìseal is a hill fort over the north-coast road, raised in the long quiet centuries and walled since. Its garrison watched the road through the Age of Strangers. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Siorrachd Caol leathan

Baile Mòr fhionn

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 18,849

Founded 6 an t-Samhain 2415 BDE by the lords of the western plain. Known for the fair citadel of the western plain.

A great fair walled city of the west, seat of lords before the kingdom and a fortress since. Its citadel was held by Ròdaich forces through the war that ended in the Severance, and it is a city of the order of the Stone. It is the chief market of the plain between the capital and the western harbours. Its own vineyards give the plain's wine, and the town salts meat, makes boots and dips candles.

  • 12 am Faoilleach 1300 BDE — The fleece-measure of Baile Mòr fhionn
  • 31 an Dàmhair 1865 DE — Wool devalued at Baile Mòr fhionn
  • 2 an Gearran 1936 DE — The houses of the Stone stand aside

Caol leathan

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,622

Founded 12 am Faoilleach 2784 BDE by the strait-pilots of the western shore. Known for strait tolls and the western pilots' guild.

Caol leathan grew on the wide strait that gives it its name, where the western pilots of the Holy Age took a toll from every boat bound for the capital's waters. Its walls and citadel were raised in the Age of Sundering to hold the strait, and were manned again when the strangers' ships began to use it after the Crossing. It is the northern anchor of the country of the Stone, and its druids look south to the temple of Lia Fàil at Inis thais for their rite.

Siorrachd Caol mhin

Caol mhin

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,648

Founded 17 am Màrt 1654 BDE by Ròdaich seafarers of Baile Mòr mhòr. Known for calm-strait harbour of Baile Mòr mhòr.

Caol mhin is the harbour of Baile Mòr mhòr on the calm strait, and its fortunes have always followed the city's. It is walled against raiders from the sea. Its quays load wool and hides from the northern uplands. Its quays stand on Eilean chrom, across the calm strait from the city.

  • 11 an Giblean 1855 DE — Quarantine at Caol mhin

Siorrachd Caol mhòr

Àth fhionn

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 844

Founded 25 an Cèitean 1793 DE by human traders, as a waystation. Known for a human waystation at the fair ford.

Àth fhionn was a waystation of human traders on the road north, built in the Age of Strangers at a fair ford. The Tuathaich kept it after the Severance. It is small, fewer than a thousand people, and its inn is still built in the humans' manner.

Àth leathan

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,686

Founded 24 am Faoilleach 886 DE by Ròdaich drovers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for a drovers' ford in the north.

The northern Àth leathan is a drovers' ford resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is not the battlefield of the Long War, which lies far to the south-west, and its people have spent a generation correcting travellers. It follows the faith of the Church.

  • 11 am Faoilleach 5784 BDE — The flint road

Baile àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,857

Founded 15 am Màrt 1348 BDE by Ròdaich shore-lords, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for old walls in the Tuathaich north.

An ancient walled town near the harbour of Caol mhòr, one of the Ròdaich towns resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. The walls are older than the Ròdaich say they know, and the Tuathaich have kept them. It follows the faith of the Church.

Baile dhubh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,709

Founded 4 an t-Samhain 1865 DE by human colliers of the northern seams. Known for coal pits of the northern holdouts.

Baile dhubh, "the black town", was built by human colliers in the Age of Strangers on one of the northern coal seams, which the humans worked alongside the vein in the south. After the Severance it passed to the Tuathaich with the rest of the north. Before the Long War it was one of the communities that refused the new fuel and kept working the last workable seams.

Caol mhòr

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 42,002

Founded 23 an Dùbhlachd 2793 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for chief harbour of the Tuathaich.

Caol mhòr, the great strait, was a Ròdaich harbour of the Holy Age. After the Severance it became the chief port of the Tuathaich, and it is now their largest town. Its yards take timber from Doire mhin, and its people keep the faith of the Church.

Caol naomh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 3,184

Founded 9 an Dàmhair 956 BDE by Ròdaich ferrymen; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the holy strait's ferry.

Caol naomh, the holy strait, is a harbour of the north-west founded by Ròdaich ferrymen in the Holy Age, who held the crossing sacred and blessed each boat before it put out. It was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance, and the new ferrymen kept the blessing without the old words. It keeps the faith of the Church.

Cnoc àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,000

Founded 19 am Màrt 2579 BDE by Ròdaich shepherds; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for hill pasture and the old cairn.

Cnoc àrsaidh is a small hill town of the Holy Age on the Abhainn mhòr, crowned by a cairn older than its name. Its Ròdaich families went south at the Severance and Tuathaich households took their holdings. It is a small place of hill pasture, looking down on the harbour of Caol mhòr.

  • 8 an Giblean 5820 BDE — The flint of Cnoc àrsaidh

Cnoc àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 704

Founded 9 an t-Samhain 986 BDE by Ròdaich hill-lords, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for an empty citadel on the southern march.

A tiny ancient hill with a citadel, far larger than the handful of people who now live in it. It was a Ròdaich keep until the Severance and has been a Tuathaich watch-post since. It follows the faith of the Church.

Cnoc bhàn

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 10,780

Founded 11 an Lùnastal 1806 BDE by Ròdaich hill-lords, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the Tuathaich southern guard-post.

A pale hill with a citadel built by a Ròdaich family in the Holy Age, taken over by the Tuathaich when their homeland was fixed. The Tuathaich garrison it as a guard-post on their southern marches, and it follows the faith of the Church. The town sells cattle and hides to Cnoc àrsaidh.

Cnoc dhubh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 8,231

Founded 5 an t-Iuchar 1683 DE by Ròdaich founders; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for the last coal pits of the north.

Cnoc dhubh is a black hill with coal seams in its flank, first dug by the Ròdaich for building-stone and later by the humans for coal. The Tuathaich who resettled it kept the pits open. It was among the northern communities that refused the dubhan economy, and its pits were the last in the north to close after the Long War.

Cuan bheag

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,782

Founded 10 am Màrt 1946 DE by Tuathaich fishing families. Known for Tuathaich fishing boats and drying racks.

Cuan bheag of the north-west was built by Tuathaich fishing families in the first years after the Severance, on a shore the Ròdaich had never settled. It is a village of boats and drying racks. It sells its catch through Caol mhòr.

  • 28 an t-Sultain 1948 DE — Boats lost off Cuan bheag

Doire mhin

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 10,048

Founded 3 an Giblean 256 BDE by Ròdaich woodsmen of the Holy Age. Known for oak timber for the Caol mhòr yards.

An oak-grove village of the Holy Age, Doire mhin was emptied of its Ròdaich families in the years of the Severance and filled by Tuathaich households moved north. It is a large village for its kind, living on the smooth-barked oaks that name it. Its timber goes down to the yards of Caol mhòr, and its people keep the faith of the Church.

  • 2 an Gearran 1935 DE — Joseph Marlow's ploughshares

Muileann fhionn

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,690

Founded 12 an t-Iuchar 1802 DE by human administrators of the northern landing. Known for strangers' fort of the north.

Muileann fhionn was built as a fort and mill by human administrators in the Age of Strangers, to guard the northern landing. After the Severance it became a Tuathaich town. It keeps the faith of the Church. Since the Severance it has been the market town of the north-western interior and the greatest cattle-market on Rodos. Its own trade is in paper and books.

  • 6 am Màrt 1920 DE — Muileann fhionn shut in
  • 12 an Giblean 1938 DE — The cattle-market at Muileann fhionn

Ros mhòr

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 8,600

Founded 15 an t-Ògmhios 393 DE by Ròdaich fishers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for big headland harbour of the Tuathaich.

Ros mhòr of the north-west is a harbour on a great headland, founded by Ròdaich fishers in the long quiet centuries. After the Severance it was resettled by the Tuathaich and grew with the northern trade. It lies between the harbours of Caol mhòr and Caol naomh.

  • 5 an Cèitean 1971 DE — Ros mhòr's boatyard

Siorrachd Caol shean

Achadh dhomhain

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,801

Founded 27 an t-Iuchar 128 BDE by hosts of the Allt an Àigh pilgrims. Known for hosts to Allt an Àigh pilgrims.

Achadh dhomhain of Caol shean is a large village beside Allt an Àigh, the stream of fortune. Pilgrims have come to drink from it since the Holy Age, and the village lives on them. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Achadh gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,649

Founded 13 an t-Ògmhios 402 BDE by the keepers of Allt an Àigh. Known for Allt an Àigh, the stream of fortune.

A rough field village beside Allt an Àigh, the stream said to grant fortune to those who drink at the right phase of the moon. Pilgrims have come since the Holy Age, and the keepers' citadel was built to guard the stream from anyone who would bottle and sell it. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith, whose druids have never agreed whether the stream's luck is real.

  • 11 an Gearran 1940 DE — The walkers at Achadh gharbh

Àth dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,250

Founded 22 an t-Samhain 1598 DE by ford-keepers of Caol shean. Known for the inland ford of Caol shean.

A deep ford on the road from Caol shean inland, where goods from the river port are loaded from boats to carts. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,640

Founded 16 an Giblean 2124 BDE by Ròdaich pilgrims to Allt an Àigh. Known for the nearest town to Allt an Àigh.

Baile dhìreach is the nearest town to Allt an Àigh, and the straight road that gives it its name runs from its square down to the stream. It grew up in the Holy Age to serve the pilgrims and still does, alongside Cnoc ìseal further up the road. Its people are wary of strangers who come at the wrong phase of the moon. Gold is washed from the stream below the town, and its refiners make blanks for the mint.

  • 19 an t-Sultain 1966 DE — The eastern blank-houses

Caol shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 31,718

Founded 21 an Lùnastal 2960 BDE by the river-fishers of the east. Known for the great eastern river port, pilgrims' landing.

An old river port on the narrows of the Abhainn ìseal, above its meeting with the Abhainn chaol, and one of the great river ports of the island, seat of Siorrachd Caol shean. It sent the ore of the central mountains down the river to Seann Mhorn when the extraction was at its height, and now sends dubhan and grain the same way. The spring of Allt an Àigh lies in its hinterland, and pilgrims to it come up the river and land here; the town follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

  • 14 an Giblean 2942 BDE — The pilgrims' path from Caol shean
  • 19 an t-Sultain 1000 DE — Caol shean's fishing year

  • 22 an Dàmhair 2010 DE — Dubhan-tùsail

Cnoc chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,719

Founded 26 an Cèitean 1814 DE by Ròdaich miners under contract. Known for abandoned shafts beneath a walled hill.

A crooked hill-town raised when the extraction contracts pushed the diggings out from the central mountains toward the coast. Its walls were thrown up against the raids of the troubles before the war, and the shafts beneath it gave out before the Severance. It is now a small town of the druid schools that sends its young to the river port at Ros fhionn.

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,278

Founded 23 an Giblean 1174 BDE by Ròdaich pilgrims to Allt an Àigh. Known for pilgrim lodgings on the Allt an Àigh road.

Cnoc ìseal began as a halt for pilgrims going down to Allt an Àigh, and its inns still fill at the phase of the moon when the stream is said to give fortune. Its nearness to Muileann chaol has drawn scholars as well, and many readers of the library lodge here. The town keeps the druid schools' habit of arguing a question before answering it.

Doire fhionn

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,551

Founded 19 an Lùnastal 2330 BDE by woodsmen of the eastern hills. Known for oak grove on the pilgrims' way.

Doire fhionn of Caol shean is an oak-grove village on the way to Allt an Àigh. Pilgrims to the stream have lodged in its houses since the Holy Age, and the Library at Muileann chaol stands on the road to the north. Its people follow the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Ros fhionn

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,377

Founded 10 am Màrt 1737 BDE by Ròdaich river-folk of the east. Known for river landing of the Allt an Àigh pilgrims.

Ros fhionn of Caol shean is a small citadel city on the Abhainn chaol in the east, near the stream of Allt an Àigh. It is where most pilgrims to the stream come ashore from the river boats that bring them up from Seann Mhorn, and its citadel was raised in the Age of Sundering to guard them. It is not the Ros fhionn of the old bridge, which lies to the north.

  • 13 an Gearran 1929 DE — The eastern pits at Ros fhionn

Siorrachd Cathair dhearg

Cathair dhearg

capital · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,274

Founded 23 an t-Samhain 2663 BDE by the custodian-kings of the Holy Age. Known for royal seat and temple of Macha.

Cathair dhearg, the red city, began as the stone-walled seat of the Holy Age custodians where the mining roads came down to the water on the Abhainn dhomhain, just above Loch chrom; Drochaid Cathair dhearg, heir of the first bridges, still carries the road across the river. It kept its walls, citadel and temple through the Sundering and the Age of Strangers, and after the Severance Rìoghachd Ròdais was declared here and Niall was crowned in it, first of the restored line. The royal precinct is small for a capital, ringed by the great harbours of Ros dhomhain, Cathair dhomhain and Baile ghlas, and its temple is the first house of Macha, where kings are made by her rite and the two horses of her rite, Liath Macha the grey and Dubh Sainglenn the black, are honoured. The royal quays build seagoing hulls for the Crown.

Siorrachd Cathair dhomhain

Cathair dhomhain

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 29,409

Founded 7 an Gearran 2755 BDE by Ròdaich shipwrights of the river mouth. Known for deep-water harbour beside the capital.

Cathair dhomhain, the deep city, stands beside the capital on the deep-water side of the river mouth, and takes the ships whose draught the royal quays cannot. It was walled and given a citadel in the Holy Age, and its temple of Macha is second only to the capital's. Its harbour carried much of the ore trade in the Age of Strangers and most of the dubhan trade since. It is the market town of the capital shore, and its own workshops bind books and put up salted food for the ships. Its quays stand where the Abhainn fhionn runs into Loch chrom, and the sea-going ships that lie at them come up from the west coast by the Abhainn gheal.

Ceann gheal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,722

Founded 8 an Gearran 1289 DE by fishers of the white headland. Known for white headland and the Toll-dubh hollow.

Ceann gheal is a harbour town north of the capital, founded in the long quiet centuries. The shaft called Toll-dubh lies in the hills behind it. Quarrymen broke into it in the Age of Sundering and found a stair cut in the rock going down beyond their lamps, and the custodians walled it up; the town's people do not go near it. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Cill ghorm

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,014

Founded 13 an t-Ògmhios 366 BDE by druids of Macha. Known for fortified temple above the capital road.

A temple site on the ridge above the road north from Cathair dhearg, fortified in the Holy Age to guard the approach to the capital. The citadel dwarfs the village, which has never numbered more than a thousand or so, most of them in service to the garrison and the shrine. Pilgrims of Òrd Mhacha, the order of Macha, stop here before entering the capital.

Siorrachd Cathair fhada

Cathair fhada

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 20,928

Founded 9 am Màrt 1239 BDE by the lords of the long city. Known for merchants of the Fèill Muileann òg.

A long walled city in the south, strung along a ridge between the capital's country and the coast, and the seat of Siorrachd Cathair fhada. It follows the order of Macha and has always been one of the capital's chief supports. The Fèill Muileann òg is held a short way north, and the city's merchants dominate it. Its market right is among the oldest on the island, and its own trade is in cheese, honey and garments.

  • 13 an Cèitean 5078 BDE — Cathair fhada on the south coast

Cnoc ruadh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,817

Founded 9 an Dàmhair 1580 DE by herders of the south road. Known for red pasture on the south road.

Cnoc ruadh of Cathair fhada is a town on the south road, a hill only in name, founded in the long quiet centuries by herders who grazed the red ground there. It grew as a stopping place between the southern ford towns and the capital. Its people keep the capital's order, the order of Macha and sell hides at the market of Àth shean.

Siorrachd Cathair mhòr

Cathair mhòr

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 49,298

Founded 30 an Giblean 2450 BDE by Ròdaich custodians of the interior roads. Known for the great city beside the old outpost.

Cathair mhòr, the great city, was raised by the Holy Age custodians beside Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, a Seann-Dhaoine outpost already in ruins when the first Ròdaich walls went up beside it. It commands the roads between the gulf and the vein country, and it was a counting-house of the tithe in the Age of Strangers and a mustering place in the war that ended it. An treas rèisimeid, raised in An Cogadh Fada, is stationed here and bears its name. Its honey and its salted meat are sold in every market of the south, and its soap-boilers and weavers are the busiest in the gulf.

Siorrachd Ceann àrsaidh

Achadh fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 9,904

Founded 21 an t-Sultain 1774 DE by Ròdaich farmers who reclaimed the wild field. Known for reclaimed wild fields.

A village of fields reclaimed from wild ground in the Age of Sundering, when the island had fewer mouths and more hands to spare. It feeds the towns of Ceann àrsaidh and sends its surplus to Muileann chrom to be ground. It is a large village now, of nearly ten thousand.

Baile chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,072

Founded 16 an Lùnastal 697 DE by Ròdaich market families of Ceann àrsaidh. Known for the bent-street market.

Baile chrom is named for its bending main street, which follows an old stream-bed. It is a market town between the capital and the northern plain, serving Baile fhiadhaich and Cuan chrom. It shares its name with three other places on the island, and the chroniclers take care to give its province.

Baile fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,925

Founded 7 an Dàmhair 368 DE by Ròdaich hunters of Ceann àrsaidh. Known for hunters and hide-curers.

The wild town was a hunters' camp in the Age of Sundering, when the forests of Ceann àrsaidh were larger. It still lives on hides and game, and its curing-sheds can be smelled from the road. Its people trade at Baile chrom.

Ceann àrsaidh

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 18,711

Founded 19 an t-Iuchar 477 BDE by Ròdaich river-folk of the east. Known for ancient headland on the capital's river road to the east.

Ceann àrsaidh is a walled river city on an ancient headland over the Abhainn fhionn, east of the capital. It has been a river port since the Holy Age, and its barges run down to Cathair dhomhain where the river runs into Loch chrom and the barges meet the ships that come up from the sea. An Taigh-seinnse Mòr stands on the road to the west.

  • 17 an t-Sultain 3273 BDE — Ceann àrsaidh
  • 19 an t-Sultain 371 BDE — The bridge at Ceann àrsaidh
  • 12 an Giblean 1830 DE — The family of Eachann Mòr
  • 3 am Màrt 1878 DE — The conclave at Ceann àrsaidh
  • 6 an Lùnastal 1929 DE — The tithe-house at Ceann àrsaidh

Cnoc bhàn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,536

Founded 5 an t-Samhain 1225 DE by druids of Macha. Known for training acolytes of Macha.

A pale hill in the midlands, crowned by a house of Òrd Mhacha, the order of the capital. The town grew around the druids' farms and remains a quiet place of tithe-barns and schools that train acolytes for the capital's temples of Macha. Baile dhomhain and Àth ghlas send it their tithes and their sons.

Cnoc ghorm

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,631

Founded 24 an t-Sultain 1152 DE by herders of Cathair mhòr. Known for horse pastures of Cathair mhòr.

A blue-grey hill town just north of Cathair mhòr, pasturing the garrison's horses. It follows the order of Macha and has always been the city's stable.

Siorrachd Ceann bheag

Achadh fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,499

Founded 10 an t-Ògmhios 726 DE by horse-breeders of the north. Known for wild-field hay and horses.

Achadh fhiadhaich is a village of the north-east, founded in the long quiet centuries on wild pasture that no earlier people had fenced. It breeds horses and grows hay for the coast, and the carters of Ceann bheag have bought its horses for generations. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Ceann bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 22,637

Founded 15 an t-Iuchar 2688 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the north-east. Known for citadel harbour of the north-east.

Ceann bheag is a citadel harbour of the north-east, a Holy Age landing that grew with the coastal trade. Its citadel was raised in the Age of Strangers to guard the anchorage the human ships used. The villages of Ceann thais and Achadh fhiadhaich lie within its province and send their goods through its quays.

  • 27 am Màrt 1922 DE — Ceann bheag stops

Ceann thais

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,605

Founded 30 an Giblean 295 DE by fishers of the north-east. Known for An Leòmhann Buidhe, the Yellow Lion.

Ceann thais is a harbour village of the north-east, best known for An Leòmhann Buidhe, one of the great taverns of the old mining circuit, which stands at its edge. It was founded in the long quiet centuries. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Ros chiar

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,614

Founded 1 an t-Iuchar 2992 BDE by the headland-lords of Ceann bheag. Known for the fortified headland harbour.

A dusky headland city on the north coast, walled, with a citadel on the rock and a harbour below. It was one of the harbours the human traders first used after the Crossing, and its citadel was taken and retaken in the war before the Severance. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and competes with Caol bheag for the northern trade. Slighe-uisce fhuar, the cold way along the north coast to Caol mhin, begins at its harbour; the grain barges of Inis mhòr sailed it until the roads took their trade.

Siorrachd Ceann leathan

Baile gheal

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,009

Founded 11 an t-Samhain 243 DE by lime-burners of Ceann leathan. Known for lime kilns of the east.

A small town of lime kilns whose white dust gives it its name. It supplies lime to the builders of the eastern coast and the fields around Ceann leathan. It keeps the Old Spirits.

Ceann leathan

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 14,116

Founded 27 am Màrt 1189 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the east. Known for broad headland harbour of the east.

Ceann leathan of the east is a harbour town and the seat of its province, founded in the Holy Age on a broad headland facing the open sea. It is not the gulf city of the melee, and its people resent the confusion. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and a fishing fleet that works as far south as the waters off Seann Bhral.

  • 25 an t-Iuchar 1826 DE — A cove burned near Ceann leathan

Siorrachd Ceann mhin

Achadh fhionn

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,747

Founded 15 an Dùbhlachd 21 DE by Ròdaich barley farmers. Known for barley fields and remount pastures.

A farming village of fair barley fields between Baile mhin and Àth ghlas. In the Age of Strangers its pastures were taken for the horses of the administration, and they have served as remount grounds for the soldiers of the district ever since. It is a quiet place, larger in fields than in people.

Àth ghlas

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,789

Founded 7 am Màrt 353 DE by Ròdaich ford-keepers. Known for grey ford that replaced the old bridge.

A small town at a grey ford upstream of Drochaid Ros fhionn. It took the traffic when the old bridge fell out of use, and grew as the bridge-villages shrank. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Caol dhomhain

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,070

Founded 8 an Gearran 1190 DE by the watch of the deep strait. Known for the deep strait's watch-tower.

Caol dhomhain is a harbour village on a deep strait of the south-east, with a citadel raised in the long quiet centuries to watch it. The village is small and the citadel is its reason. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Ceann mhin

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 32,321

Founded 18 an Lùnastal 2254 BDE by shipwrights of the smooth headland. Known for shipyards of the smooth headland.

Ceann mhin is a citadel harbour on the southern gulf shore, long the chief shipyard of the east. When Tonn Mhòr struck in the first years of the restored kingdom, its yards were spared and it took in the survivors of Achadh mhin. It has since grown into one of the great cities of the south. The hemp for its yards grows in its own fields, and its copyists bind books for the south.

Ceann mhin

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 19,533

Founded 12 an t-Iuchar 1336 BDE by harbour-lords of the smooth headland. Known for the northern ore harbour.

A smooth headland port, walled, and the seat of Siorrachd Ceann mhin. It was a trading harbour for the northern mines in the Age of Strangers and follows the druid schools of the Old Faith. Slighe Ceann mhin, the long road down the east of the island to Seann Dunn, begins at its gate.

Ceann mhin

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 19,395

Founded 17 an t-Iuchar 220 BDE by Ròdaich fishers settling in the ruin of Làrach an Dùin. Known for harbour beneath Làrach an Dùin.

Ceann mhin is built in and around Làrach an Dùin, the ruined fortress of the old builders, and its harbour lies under the fallen walls. The Ròdaich fishers who settled there in the Holy Age reused its stones but never finished clearing it; nobody knows who built the fortress. It is now a walled port town of nearly twenty thousand, the seat of its province, and the rival of Ceann chaol along the same coast.

  • 26 an Dùbhlachd 4573 BDE — Ceann mhin on the south-eastern shore
  • 12 an t-Ògmhios 183 BDE — Anna Ruadh at Ceann mhin

Cnoc dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,252

Founded 20 an Lùnastal 2977 BDE by Ròdaich keepers of Tuam Cnoc dhìreach. Known for keepers of Tuam Cnoc dhìreach.

A small town on the Sìtheas beside Tuam Cnoc dhìreach, the necropolis whose oldest graves are older than its oldest legible names. Its families have kept the necropolis since the Holy Age, when it received its first formally recorded burial. It lives on the burials of the eastern coast and on the masons who cut the stones.

  • 26 an t-Ògmhios 2805 BDE — The grave-keepers of Cnoc dhìreach

Cnoc fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,584

Founded 2 an t-Samhain 1769 DE by hunters of the north-east hills. Known for game and hides for Ceann mhin.

A wild hill above Ceann mhin, settled by hunters and later by carters on the harbour road. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and sends game and hides down to the port.

Cnoc ghorm

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 16,474

Founded 30 am Faoilleach 707 BDE by Ròdaich keepers of Calbh Cnoc ghorm. Known for the doctrine stone.

The blue hill grew up around Calbh Cnoc ghorm, the standing column carved with the doctrine itself: Cha do thàinig sinn; bha sinn ann. If the doctrine has a birthplace it may be here, and the town has never let the island forget it. It is a large town now, and pilgrims of all three faiths climb to the stone.

  • 17 an Giblean 7992 BDE — The gatherings at the column
  • 25 an Lùnastal 1929 DE — The fight at Cnoc ghorm

Cnoc thais

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,511

Founded 3 an t-Iuchar 497 DE by hill-farmers of the south-east. Known for cattle on a misty hill.

A damp hill above the small harbour of Caol dhomhain in the south-east. It keeps the Old Spirits and sends its cattle to Baile gheal.

Muileann leathan

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,802

Founded 16 an Dàmhair 1384 DE by millers of Ceann mhin. Known for broad mill serving Ceann mhin.

A walled mill town a short way inland from Ceann mhin, whose broad mill-pool is the largest on that coast. It was walled when Ceann mhin was, in the Age of Strangers, to protect its stores. Its flour goes to the ships at Ceann mhin and never to the rival quays of Ceann chaol.

Seann Bhrenn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,695

Founded 15 an Lùnastal 12,144 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for old harbour quarrelling with Caol gharbh.

Seann Bhrenn is an old harbour of the Seann-Dhaoine, settled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. It lies hard beside Caol gharbh, and the two harbours have quarrelled over the same water for as long as there are records, each claiming the other was built on its fishing ground. It is a port town of nearly nine thousand and the older of the two by its name.

  • 5 an Giblean 10,798 BDE — The twin landings of Seann Bhrenn

Siorrachd Ceann mhòr

Àth dhearg

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 5,681

Founded 15 an Giblean 1090 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for red ford under the Baile chrom light.

A red ford on the western coast below the lighthouse of Baile chrom, struck by Gorta Baile chrom in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its people keep the faith of the Church, as most of this coast does. It is not the Àth dhearg of the north-eastern lighthouse.

Àth fhionn

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 8,986

Founded 14 an Dùbhlachd 1224 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for fair ford of the western coast.

A fair ford on the western coast road below the lighthouse of Baile chrom, struck by Gorta Baile chrom in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is a town of nearly nine thousand and the market for Doire chaol's charcoal. Its people follow the faith of the Church, as most of this coast does.

Ceann mhòr

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 32,420

Founded 6 an Cèitean 2836 BDE by Ròdaich fishers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for great headland harbour under the Baile chrom light.

Ceann mhòr is a great harbour on a headland of the north-west, under the beacon of Taigh-solais Baile chrom. It was a Ròdaich port of the Holy Age, struck by Gorta Baile chrom in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It keeps the faith of the Church. Its first human fishing families learned their church's harbour prayers here, and its priests say the Grey Night vigil of Baile chrom began from them. It has been the market town of the north-west coast since the shires were drawn, and it sends fish, whale-oil, seal-oil, amber, dyes and tobacco south. Glass is blown from the white sand of its beaches.

Cill ìseal

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 15,029

Founded 14 an t-Iuchar 896 DE by Ròdaich shrine-keepers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the church of the north-west.

A low church-site village of the Ròdaich, emptied at the Severance and resettled by Tuathaich families. It has grown past any village size, with its church at its heart, and it farms for the harbour of Ros ruadh. The Tuathaich here call it by its Ròdaich name and no other.

Doire chaol

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,560

Founded 28 an Dùbhlachd 1195 DE by Ròdaich charcoal-burners; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for narrow oakwood and charcoal.

A charcoal village in a narrow oakwood, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. The newcomers made the Ròdaich shrine of Manannan they found there their church rather than raising their own, as several villages of this coast did. It still burns charcoal for the smiths of Àth fhionn and Àth dhearg.

Ros ruadh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 7,782

Founded 29 an t-Iuchar 1636 DE by Ròdaich fishers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the Naomh Breandan telling of the north-west.

A red headland harbour on the north-west coast, one of the Ròdaich harbours given to the Tuathaich after the Severance. The fishing families of Ros ruadh are among those who keep the voyage of Naomh Breandan alive in speech, and some say the saint's boat put out from this headland. It follows the faith of the Church.

  • 29 an Dàmhair 9840 BDE — Seven boats lost off Ros ruadh

Siorrachd Cill dhìreach

Baile bhàn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,156

Founded 30 an t-Sultain 1229 DE by a custodian house of Cill dhìreach. Known for citadel above Cill dhìreach.

Baile bhàn is a white town with a citadel above Cill dhìreach, built to guard the temple-town and its treasuries. It is a town of five thousand. Its garrison keeps order at Còmhrag Ceann leathan.

Cill dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 24,187

Founded 12 am Màrt 400 BDE by druids of Macha. Known for temple-town of the Ceann leathan melee.

Cill dhìreach is a temple village of Macha of twenty-four thousand and the seat of its province. It lies beside Ceann leathan, where Còmhrag Ceann leathan is held each year. Its druids tend the wounded of the melee and bury its dead.

  • 19 an t-Sultain 1851 DE — The shrine at Cill dhìreach

Siorrachd Cill thais

Baile ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,818

Founded 1 an t-Sultain 788 DE by farmers of Cill thais. Known for small walls near the capital.

A small walled town near Cill thais and Baile chiar, west of the capital. The walls were raised in the war before the Severance. It follows the order of Macha and has little trade of its own.

Cill thais

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 18,934

Founded 15 an t-Samhain 1066 BDE by wardens of the sacred wood. Known for wardens of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag.

Cill thais, the damp cell, is a large village and the seat of its province, founded in the Holy Age beside Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag. The forest is sacred to Macha and her black horse and has never been settled, logged or fully mapped, and the village's wardens keep others out of it under the division of custody that settled the holy-wood dispute. In the Age of Strangers the wardens refused the timber contracts, and the record does not say how they were allowed to.

  • 6 an t-Iuchar 1806 DE — The orphans of Cill thais

Cnoc bheag

fort · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,455

Founded 26 an t-Ògmhios 1865 BDE by custodians named in the holy-wood dispute. Known for fort at the edge of the holy wood.

Cnoc bheag is a fort with a citadel at the edge of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, the forest that has never been settled or logged. It was raised after the holy-wood dispute of the Holy Age, when custody of the wood was divided rather than awarded, to house the custodians of the share that went to the order now called Òrd Mhacha, the order of Macha. It stands outside the trees, never within them, and its twelve thousand people guard the capital's south as well as the wood.

Cnoc àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 16,832

Founded 11 am Màrt 1238 BDE by Ròdaich followers of the order of the Stone. Known for shrines of the Stone and the panther watch.

Cnoc àrsaidh is a walled town of Òrd na Cloiche and the seat of its province, holding the oldest shrines of the order of the Stone. The panther roads pass close by, and the town keeps a watch on them in the season of crossing. Its walls were raised in the Age of Strangers and have not been needed since.

Cnoc uaine

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,930

Founded 31 an t-Iuchar 1116 DE by hill-lords of the south-west. Known for the walled green hill.

A green walled hill in the south-west, fortified against pirates who raided the coast in the centuries after the Sundering. It follows the order of the Stone and sends its young to the first fleet at Àth gharbh.

Siorrachd Cnoc bhàn

Baile thais

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,570

Founded 28 an Cèitean 816 BDE by Ròdaich eel-fishers of the water-meadows. Known for water-meadows and eel traps.

Baile thais stands on damp ground where the meadows flood each wet season, and its people have always fished the ditches for eels. It is a large town now, and it supplies Cnoc bhàn with hay and fish. The river works that keep the meadows are older than the town's charter.

Ceann dhomhain

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,589

Founded 7 am Màrt 1257 BDE by custodians of the eastern headland. Known for the library's river landing and cargo registers.

A small city on a headland over a deep reach of the Abhainn naomh, with a citadel that looks down the river toward the sea and back toward the mountain roads. River boats put in here with the cargoes landed at Ceann mhin, at the river mouth, for the library town of Muileann chaol, whose scholars and copyists travel through its gate, and its quay-masters have long kept a copy of every cargo list for the Leabharlann. The druid schools hold the city, and its scholars are counted among the library's oldest correspondents.

Cnoc bhàn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 16,069

Founded 12 am Màrt 2717 BDE by a custodian house of the Binding. Known for white citadel and the druid schools' disputations.

The white hill was fortified early by a custodian house, and its citadel of pale stone is the oldest standing work in the province that bears its name. In the Age of Strangers it served as a district seat of the human administration, and the ledgers kept in its strong-room were among those later lost in the war. It is now a large town of scholars and advocates: the disputations of the druid schools are held in its hall, and its readers walk daily to the library at Muileann chaol.

  • 28 an Gearran 709 BDE — The strike-books compared

Doire dhubh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,158

Founded 26 an Dùbhlachd 476 BDE by Ròdaich woodwards of Cnoc bhàn. Known for dark oak for the library's shelves.

A village in a dark oak grove a short way north of Muileann chaol. When the library was founded its oak was cut for the shelves and reading-tables, and the woodwards still claim a right to repair them. It sends its remaining timber to Cnoc bhàn and Baile thais.

Muileann chaol

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,706

Founded 12 am Màrt 429 BDE by grain-millers of the Holy Age. Known for the library's misaddressed parcels.

The smaller and older of the two Muileann chaols, a narrow mill beside a small keep in the eastern hills. The great library stands in its namesake to the south-east, and the library's carriers are said still to bring misaddressed parcels here. It is a town of the druid schools, and its mill feeds the villages of Achadh gharbh and Tobar dhubh.

  • 5 am Faoilleach 1904 DE — The second Muileann chaol

Muileann chaol

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,496

Founded 24 an Dùbhlachd 469 DE by millers of the narrow race. Known for Leabharlann Muileann chaol, the great library.

A narrow mill town in the eastern hills, and the home of Leabharlann Muileann chaol, the library that keeps the most complete record of the island. The library was founded in the new kingdom and has since taken in the provincial archives, and its war archive is sealed. The town lives on the library and on the river landing at Ceann dhomhain, and to put a thing in the Library is to settle it. Paper has been made here since the Age of Sundering, and its copyists and binders work for the library.

Muileann fhada

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,719

Founded 21 an Giblean 1759 BDE by millers of the Ros fhionn river. Known for a river port gone quiet.

A long mill-house on the Ros fhionn gave the place its name, and a river quay below it made it a port, sending flour downstream by barge. Its walls date from the Age of Strangers, when a tithe store was kept here and needed guarding. Trade on the river dried up when the carts took the traffic, and the crossing of Drochaid Ros fhionn just upstream is now rarely used; the town has shrunk to its walls.

Tobar dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,108

Founded 25 an t-Iuchar 362 DE by well-diggers of Baile thais. Known for the straight water-channel.

A large well village in the central-east, laid out along a straight channel that carries its water. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and supplies water and vegetables to Baile Mòr uaine and Baile thais. Its paper-mill makes the paper of the royal chronicle.

Tobar dhubh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,743

Founded 7 an t-Samhain 1409 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers of Cnoc bhàn. Known for the dark well of old telling.

A village around a deep well whose water runs dark, said in the old telling to rise from near the vein. It has never been proved so, and the druid scholars of Cnoc bhàn have argued it both ways. The well still draws visitors who drink from it for luck.

Siorrachd Cnoc bheag

Achadh fhada

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,174

Founded 31 an Cèitean 625 DE by druids of the Hungry Hawk. Known for the Hawk-order fields.

A long field village in the wooded middle west, one of the few settlements where Òrd an t-Seabhaig, the Hawk order, whose rite is the older form of Òrd Bhrìde's, still holds. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck it in the Age of Strangers. Its fields feed the Hawk-order mill at Muileann uaine.

Achadh mhòr

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,399

Founded 28 an Gearran 143 BDE by Ròdaich farmers of Cnoc bheag. Known for border fields south of the Tuathaich line.

A farming village of six thousand just south of the Tuathaich line. It follows the order of Manannan, like its neighbours across the line. It trades with both sides and has been watched by both.

Baile dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,324

Founded 2 an t-Samhain 1101 DE by Ròdaich followers of the Hawk order. Known for walled deep-valley town of the Hawk order.

Baile dhomhain is a walled town in a deep valley near Cnoc bheag, one of the towns of the Hawk order. Its walls were raised in the Age of Strangers and strengthened after the Severance, when the Tuathaich line was drawn close by. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck it in the Age of Strangers. Its trade goes down to the quay at Ceann òg.

Ceann òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,349

Founded 19 an t-Sultain 1787 DE by Ròdaich and human traders together. Known for young river quay near Carragh Cnoc bheag.

Ceann òg, "the young headland", was built as a river trading quay on the Abhainn ìseal in the first years after the Crossing, when exchange with the humans was still reciprocal. It stands near Carragh Cnoc bheag, the stone carved Bha teine sa chloich. The Green Death, A' Phlàigh Uaine, struck it in the Age of Strangers. It follows the Hawk order, and its quay was rebuilt after the Severance for Ròdaich boats alone. Seòlaid Ceann òg, the western lane round the capes to the capital's water, is named for its quay.

  • 23 an Giblean 1808 DE — Seòlaid Ceann òg

Cnoc bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 49,661

Founded 10 an Dàmhair 1401 BDE by hill kindreds of the north-central country. Known for the carved stone and the Sixth Regiment.

Cnoc bheag is the small hill only in name: it is the largest town of the north-central country, a river port on the Abhainn ìseal whose barges run down to Ros gheal on the coast, and the heart of the Hawk order of the Old Faith, whose temple here is the chief house of the Hawk of Acaill. The standing stone Carragh Cnoc bheag, carved 'there was fire in the stone', stands a short walk to the south, and the town's older families say their fathers' fathers found it there. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck the town in the Age of Strangers. Since the Severance it has faced the Tuathaich border, and An siathamh rèisimeid, raised in An Cogadh Fada, is stationed here under the town's name.

Inis ìseal

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,217

Founded 11 an Dùbhlachd 820 DE by the garrison of Cnoc bheag. Known for island fortress guarding Cnoc bheag.

Inis ìseal is a low island in the Abhainn ìseal above Cnoc bheag, fortified in the long quiet centuries to guard that town's river and walled again in the Age of Strangers. Since the Severance it has been a frontier fortress facing the Tuathaich border, supplied by boats that come up the river from Ros gheal. The Green Death, A' Phlàigh Uaine, struck its garrison in the Age of Strangers, and it is a city by rank and a barracks in practice. The fortress keeps its own boatyard and weaving-sheds, and its cheese goes down the river to Ros gheal.

Muileann uaine

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,601

Founded 3 an t-Sultain 406 BDE by druids of the Hungry Hawk. Known for the Hawk-order mill.

A green mill in the wooded middle west, one of the few towns where Òrd an t-Seabhaig, the Hawk order, whose rite is the older form of Òrd Bhrìde's, still holds. The carved hawk over the mill-door is said to be as old as the Binding of the First Flame. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck it in the Age of Strangers, and since then the second sense of 'uaine' has clung to its name.

Ros dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,232

Founded 30 an Lùnastal 586 DE by fishers of the Hawk coast. Known for walled fishing village of the Hawk coast.

Ros dhìreach of Cnoc bheag is a walled fishing village on the north-central coast, founded in the long quiet centuries. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck it in the Age of Strangers. It was walled after the Severance, when the Tuathaich coast became a frontier. It keeps the rite of the Hawk order.

Tobar dhomhain

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 665

Founded 17 am Màrt 1811 DE by miners of the western hills. Known for the well of a lost camp.

A deep well-village in the western hills, dug to supply a mining camp that has since been abandoned. It is one of the smallest villages on the island and follows the order of Manannan. The grassland above the village is where the Leaden Hawk company kept its watch on the road from Ros bheag in the first spring of the Severance war.

  • 23 an Giblean 1929 DE — The watch in the grasslands

Siorrachd Cnoc dhìreach

Cnoc dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 18,778

Founded 21 an Lùnastal 817 DE by a custodian house of the eastern diggings. Known for walled seat of the mining district.

Cnoc dhìreach is the walled seat of the eastern mining district, a town of nearly nineteen thousand. It was walled in the Age of Strangers, when the strikes in the district made the administration nervous. It is not the small town of the necropolis on the south-east coast.

  • 18 an Dàmhair 133 BDE — Cnoc dhìreach's weavers
  • 12 an Lùnastal 1918 DE — The signatories of Cnoc dhìreach

Doire gharbh

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 12,662

Founded 5 an t-Iuchar 1230 DE by Ròdaich woodwards of Cnoc dhìreach. Known for palisade under the Doire uaine hills.

A large village in rough oakwood below the Doire uaine hills, walled against the thing that the old inscriptions say walks in those hills. The record gives a more ordinary reason: the walls went up in the Age of Strangers, when the strikes in the eastern district reached its gates. The warm springs of Muileann ruadh lie a short walk east.

Siorrachd Cnoc dhubh

Àth uaine

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 4,214

Founded 6 an Cèitean 1842 DE by Ròdaich miners under extraction contract. Known for camp graves by the green ford.

Àth uaine of Cnoc dhubh began as a mining camp at a ford in the Age of Strangers. Its camp graves lie in the field by the ford, tended by the keepers of the Old Spirits' ancestor rite. The camp outlived its working and became a small farm town.

Baile òg

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,898

Founded 7 an Dàmhair 479 DE by stone-gatherers of the temple hills. Known for houses of stone from Làrach an Teampaill.

A young town in the eastern hills close by the ruins of Làrach an Teampaill, whose altar faces the vein. Its early houses were built of stones carried off the ruins, a use the elders of the Old Spirits later forbade. It keeps the Old Spirits and serves travellers who come to look at the ruins.

Ceann ghorm

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,761

Founded 29 an Giblean 356 DE by river pilots of the east. Known for river pilots of the Abhainn chaol.

Ceann ghorm, the blue headland, is a river town on the Abhainn chaol in the east whose pilots have long guided boats up from Seann Mhorn on the coast to the landings of Seann Dunn and Ros fhionn. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and grew in the Age of Strangers. Its people follow the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Cnoc àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,738

Founded 20 an t-Iuchar 371 DE by hill-farmers from Cnoc dhubh. Known for the summit cairn and eastern barley.

The 'ancient hill' of the eastern cluster of Cnocs is in fact among the younger of them; the chroniclers think the name was taken from a cairn on its summit rather than from the town. It is a small farming town of the druid schools that sells its barley in Cnoc dhubh and Àth dhomhain.

Cnoc bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,621

Founded 5 an Dàmhair 988 DE by shepherds of Cnoc dhubh. Known for shepherds' market below Cnoc dhubh.

A small hill town below Cnoc dhubh, holding the shepherds' market for the province. It has always been a dependent of the larger town. It is one of several places named Cnoc bheag and is not the fort of the holy wood near the capital.

Cnoc dhubh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,141

Founded 10 an t-Iuchar 601 DE by charcoal-burners of the black hill. Known for charcoal for the smithies.

A black hill where charcoal burners worked through the long centuries of the Sundering, the Small-Burning Law forbidding them the ore. It is the largest of the cluster of Cnocs in the eastern hills and their common market. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith, and its charcoal is still sold to smiths who will not work with dubhan.

Cnoc dhubh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,389

Founded 2 am Faoilleach 2734 BDE by a custodian house that quarried the black hill. Known for black-stone quarries and walled market.

The black hill is an outcrop of dark stone that the early custodians hoped was the vein; it was not, and the quarry that tested it became a town. Cnoc dhubh is a walled market for the herders and quarrymen of the hills near Làrach an Teampaill; the seat of the shire is the other Cnoc dhubh, the charcoal-burners' town. Prospectors dug here again in the Age of Strangers and found only rock, a result the town's chroniclers record with some satisfaction.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,884

Founded 8 an Dùbhlachd 1860 DE by miners' families from Cnoc dhubh. Known for overflow houses of Cnoc dhubh.

The 'young hill' was settled by families spilling out of Cnoc dhubh when the mass excavation drew workers to the eastern hills. It has little of its own beyond houses and a meeting-hall of the druid schools, and its people work in the fields and shops of its larger neighbour.

Doire bhàn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,141

Founded 14 an t-Iuchar 13 BDE by the oak-cutters of Seann Dunn. Known for timber for the coast harbours.

A white oak grove between Seann Dunn and Seann Mhorn, cut for charcoal and ship-timber. It keeps the Old Spirits and is a large, quiet village with no walls.

Doire fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 16,332

Founded 13 an t-Samhain 1651 BDE by custodians of Cnoc dhubh. Known for citadel village of Cnoc dhubh.

Doire fhiadhaich of Cnoc dhubh is a village only by the old rank; it is large, and it has a citadel raised by the Holy Age custodians who held these hills. Làrach an Teampaill lies in the hills to its east. Its people keep the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and will not cut the oaks nearest the ruin.

Doire ghlas

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 7,971

Founded 14 an Gearran 2496 BDE by woodsmen of Cnoc dhubh. Known for grey oaks by Làrach an Teampaill.

Doire ghlas of Cnoc dhubh is a village of grey oaks near Làrach an Teampaill. It was founded in the Holy Age, and its people have guided visitors to the ruin ever since. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Inis uaine

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 5,290

Founded 3 an t-Ògmhios 941 DE by boatmen of the Abhainn chaol. Known for barracks of the Eighth Regiment.

Inis uaine is a river town on a green island in the Abhainn chaol in the east, founded in the long quiet centuries; its boats go down to the sea at Seann Mhorn. In An Cogadh Fada, An t-ochdamh rèisimeid was raised here to guard the eastern dubhan tanks and took the town's name, and the barracks have changed the town's trade from fish to soldiers' wants. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

  • 14 an Dùbhlachd 2024 DE — The eighth regiment at Inis uaine

Muileann gharbh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,475

Founded 12 am Màrt 1812 DE by a human ore concern. Known for rough mill of the ore road.

Muileann gharbh, the rough mill, was built in the Age of Strangers to crush ore on the road down to the eastern harbours. When the mountain was worked day and night the mill never stopped, and the town grew no larger than the mill needed. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith, whose teachers found many hearers among the mill hands.

Muileann leathan

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 7,664

Founded 15 an Dùbhlachd 1253 BDE by the millers of the wide stream. Known for wide mill-wheels, grain for Seann Mhorn.

A broad mill on a slow river, old enough that its founding is recorded only in the king-lists of the Holy Age. It grinds for the coast-town of Seann Mhorn and for the villages round Àth àrsaidh, and its people keep the Old Spirits. The temple ruins of Làrach an Teampaill lie in the hills behind it, and the millers will not quarry them.

Seann Dunn

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 15,318

Founded 5 an Cèitean 10,435 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for An Taigh-seinnse Òir and the temple road.

Seann Dunn keeps a Seann-Dhaoine name, and its citadel stands on footings no Ròdaich mason laid. It stands on the Abhainn chaol a little above the river mouth, and is the river landing and lodging-place for those who visit Làrach an Teampaill in the hills to the north, whose ships put in at Seann Mhorn down the coast; its own ancestor hall serves the Old Spirits. An Taigh-seinnse Òir, one of the great taverns of the old mining circuit, stands in the town itself. Its yards are the largest shipyard on Rodos, and the town cuts the sails and makes the cheese of the east coast. Slighe-mhara àrsaidh, the ancient sea-way of the Old Ones, begins at the river mouth below the town and runs round the south-east cape to Ceann chaol.

Seann Mhorn

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 5,044

Founded 5 an t-Iuchar 12,516 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for Seann-Dhaoine stones in the harbour wall.

The Seann-Dhaoine left the harbour-stones and the name Morn; the Ròdaich, finding both, called the place Seann Mhorn and built on top. It is a walled port with a citadel over the harbour mouth, fought over more than once in the troubles before the Severance, and it keeps the Old Spirits of the Ròdaich. Stones of the older builders are set into the harbour wall, and the fishermen touch one before they sail.

Tobar shean

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,420

Founded 29 an Lùnastal 783 DE by well-keepers of Baile òg. Known for the walled well on the temple road.

An old well-village in the eastern hills, walled in the troubled years because its well was the only sure water on the road past Làrach an Teampaill. It keeps the Old Spirits, and the well-keepers still close the gate in dry seasons and ration the water by the bucket.

Siorrachd Cnoc gheal

Àth dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 8,302

Founded 19 an Dùbhlachd 2635 BDE by ford-keepers of the north-east coast. Known for Taigh-solais Àth dhearg, the north-east beacon.

A red ford-town near the north-east coast, whose name was given to Taigh-solais Àth dhearg, one of the five lighthouses built in the Age of Strangers at the request of human navigators. The beacon burned the ore for more than a century and was among the first things on the island converted to dubhan. The town keeps the Old Spirits and lives by the coast road and the lighthouse.

  • 28 an Cèitean 1825 DE — Àth dhearg builds the tower

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,843

Founded 6 am Màrt 1115 DE by road-builders of Cnoc gheal. Known for the straight road to Seann Bhrenn.

A straight town on the road from Cnoc gheal to Seann Bhrenn, named for the road that made it. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and is a carters' stop on the way to the coast.

Baile fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,834

Founded 6 am Faoilleach 563 DE by farmers of the north-east. Known for walled farm town of the north-east.

Baile fhiadhaich of Cnoc gheal is a walled farm town of the north-east. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and walled in the Age of Strangers against raiders from the sea. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. Its fields grow the dye-plants of the north-east, and its colours go to the feast-market at Seann Tarr.

Cnoc gheal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 14,488

Founded 5 an t-Iuchar 71 BDE by hill-farmers of the north-east. Known for the white hill market of the north-east.

A white hill in the north-east, seat of Siorrachd Cnoc gheal, looking down on the Seann-Dhaoine harbour of Seann Bhrenn. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and is the market for Baile dhìreach and Àth dhearg.

  • 27 am Màrt 1922 DE — The quarrymen of Cnoc gheal

Seann Tarr

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,869

Founded 17 an Lùnastal 8218 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the Old Ones' landing stones.

Seann Tarr is a small harbour whose landing stones are older than any Ròdaich work, and the root in its name is not Gaelic. Ròdaich fishers settled it in the Holy Age and gave it the name it bears, marking it as a place of the Old Ones. On clear nights the lighthouse of Àth dhearg can be seen from its quay, and its boats steer by it.

  • 2 an t-Iuchar 7173 BDE — The count at Seann Tarr

Tobar bhàn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 4,449

Founded 13 an Cèitean 2031 BDE by well-keepers of the north-eastern shore road. Known for white well and the lighthouse keepers.

Tobar bhàn is a well village on the north-eastern shore road, named for a spring whose water runs white with chalk. The beacon of Taigh-solais Àth dhearg stands on the coast beyond it, and through the later Age of Strangers the village kept the lamp-keepers in bread and peat. Its people hold to the Old Spirits, the ancestors and the weather, and still leave a cup at the well before a sea-journey.

Siorrachd Cnoc ghorm

Àth fhada

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 15,665

Founded 18 am Màrt 869 DE by Ròdaich ford-wardens, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the long ford and its toll.

A long ford on the north-western roads, held by a Ròdaich warden-family through the quiet centuries of the Sundering. After the Severance its houses were emptied and given to Tuathaich families shepherded north, who raised the present walls and made it one of the chief towns of their homeland. The Tuathaich here keep the faith of the Church, and their church stands among the shrines the Ròdaich left behind; the ford is still paid for in toll. Its dubhan works, the largest in the north-west, is now its chief trade, and it binds books, a craft the Tuathaich learned at Muileann leathan.

  • 26 am Faoilleach 1970 DE — The Tuathaich carters' road

Àth uaine

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 10,109

Founded 18 an t-Samhain 823 BDE by Ròdaich weavers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for green ford and flax-weaving.

Àth uaine of Cnoc ghorm is a green ford of the north-west, founded by Ròdaich flax-weavers in the Holy Age. It was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance and still weaves. It keeps the faith of the Church.

Baile dhubh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,262

Founded 22 an Dàmhair 1103 DE by Ròdaich herders of the black-soil fields. Known for Ròdaich enclave on the Tuathaich border.

Named for the dark earth of its fields, Baile dhubh was an ordinary Ròdaich farm town until the Severance drew the northern border around it. It kept its people when the province of Cnoc ghorm passed to the Tuathaich, and has lived since as a place of exchange and quiet mutual suspicion. Its folk keep the Old Faith in the order of Manannan, whose sea-feasts their Christian neighbours to the north have always kept beside their own, which is thought to be why they were left in peace.

Ceann dhubh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 3,075

Founded 25 an Cèitean 1257 BDE by Ròdaich headland-fishers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the black headland beside Inis àrsaidh.

A black headland harbour on the north-west coast, all but joined to the city of Inis àrsaidh. It was a Ròdaich fishing town until the Severance and has been a Tuathaich harbour since. It follows the faith of the Church, and its boats sail with Inis àrsaidh's.

Cnoc ghorm

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 25,112

Founded 15 an Dàmhair 717 BDE by Ròdaich farmers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for inland seat of the Tuathaich.

Cnoc ghorm of the north-west is the inland seat of its province and one of the largest Tuathaich towns. It was a Ròdaich farm town of the Holy Age, resettled after the Severance. It is not the place of the stone Calbh Cnoc ghorm, which lies far to the south-east. Its dye-fields and smithies are the busiest in the Tuathaich north.

  • 25 am Màrt 6222 BDE — Cattle in the north-west
  • 26 an t-Ògmhios 1829 DE — Human farms at Cnoc ghorm
  • 30 am Màrt 1938 DE — The churches of the north
  • 29 an Giblean 1939 DE — The church school at Cnoc ghorm
  • 11 an Gearran 1955 DE — The northern sea-feast

Inis àrsaidh

city · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,740

Founded 28 an t-Sultain 2757 BDE by Ròdaich island-lords, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the Tuathaich island harbour.

An ancient island city on the north-west coast, all but joined to Ceann dhubh. It was a Ròdaich harbour-city until the Severance and has been Tuathaich since. It follows the faith of the Church and is one of the few Tuathaich harbours with a fleet of its own.

  • 10 an t-Iuchar 1931 DE — The north-west ports without a master

Siorrachd Cnoc leathan

Àth ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,610

Founded 27 an Lùnastal 390 DE by Ròdaich innkeepers of Cnoc leathan. Known for blue ford by An Taigh-òsta Grianach.

A small town at a blue ford a short way from An Taigh-òsta Grianach, the great roadside inn of the eastern circuit. Its people keep stables and sell to travellers. It fortified its inns before the war, as the tavern road did everywhere.

Cnoc dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,850

Founded 18 an Dàmhair 1200 DE by tavern-keepers of the eastern road. Known for An Taigh-òsta Grianach.

A straight hill on the mining road in the south-east, home of An Taigh-òsta Grianach, a famous roadside inn that serves pan-fried spinach with black wine. The inn was fortified as a militia waypoint in the troubles before the Severance and took dubhan lamps with the rest of the tavern circuit. It keeps the Old Spirits and lies close by the ruins of Làrach an Dùin.

Cnoc leathan

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 24,072

Founded 11 am Màrt 2827 BDE by innkeepers of the south road. Known for An Taigh-òsta Grianach on the south road.

Cnoc leathan is a large town and the seat of its province, on the south road of the east. An Taigh-òsta Grianach, one of the great inns of the old circuit, stands to its south. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. Slighe Cnoc leathan, the road south past An Taigh-òsta Grianach, has been kept up by the inn's own toll since Anna Ruadh's charter.

  • 1 an Gearran 2390 BDE — Cnoc leathan's market
  • 1 an Gearran 1929 DE — Cnoc leathan's riflemen
  • 21 an Giblean 1979 DE — Cnoc leathan's schools

Cnoc thais

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 11,502

Founded 20 an Dùbhlachd 235 DE by reed-cutters of Cnoc leathan. Known for reed-cutters and thatch.

Cnoc thais is a damp hill whose reed-beds thatch the roofs of the eastern plain. It is a town of eleven thousand. Its cutters work the beds in the dry months and its thatchers travel in the wet.

Muileann ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 4,133

Founded 15 am Faoilleach 151 DE by Ròdaich millers of Cnoc leathan. Known for red mill on the inn road.

Muileann ruadh is a walled mill town near An Taigh-òsta Grianach, the great inn of the eastern road. Its walls were raised when the inns fortified before the war, and the town and the inn have shared a watch ever since. The eastern Toll-dubh, the shaft of the Old Ones that charcoal-burners found again in the Age of Sundering and the custodians walled up, lies close by, and the townsfolk keep away from it. It is not the Muileann ruadh of the warm springs to the west.

Siorrachd Cnoc mhòr

Cnoc chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,718

Founded 23 an Lùnastal 1923 DE by the ore-carriers of the interior. Known for walled depot of the ore road.

Cnoc chrom was built in the Age of Strangers as a depot on the ore road from the interior to the gulf. It was walled in the years before the war of the Severance, when the mining roads began to arm themselves. It is a small town now and keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Cnoc mhòr

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 25,190

Founded 8 am Màrt 1789 BDE by cattle-drovers of the interior. Known for cattle market below Cathair mhòr.

Cnoc mhòr is the market hill on the Abhainn chiar below Cathair mhòr, where the interior drove roads meet. It was walled in the Age of Strangers, when the city's markets spilled out to it. It is a prosperous town that keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha and sells the gulf its beef.

  • 19 an t-Samhain 574 BDE — The granary of Cnoc mhòr
  • 14 an Lùnastal 1817 DE — Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr

Ros dhìreach

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,452

Founded 22 an t-Ògmhios 37 DE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the gulf. Known for straight headland harbour.

Ros dhìreach of Cnoc mhòr is a harbour on a straight headland of the gulf, founded in the long quiet centuries. It is a city by rank and the harbour of Cnoc mhòr's cattle trade. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha. Its clay-pits feed its potteries, and its soap-boilers serve the gulf.

  • 15 an Dùbhlachd 1849 DE — Ros dhìreach the second ore port
  • 27 an t-Iuchar 1894 DE — The tram-road to Ros dhìreach

Siorrachd Cnoc naomh

Achadh mhin

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,463

Founded 1 an Lùnastal 2261 BDE by farmers of the southern coast. Known for rebuilt after the Great Wave.

Achadh mhin is a farming village of the south, founded in the Holy Age. Tonn Mhòr struck it in the first years of the restored kingdom and destroyed it in a single night. It was rebuilt and keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

  • 6 an Dùbhlachd 1933 DE — Achadh mhin under salt
  • 13 am Faoilleach 1957 DE — Achadh mhin resettled

Cnoc naomh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 19,961

Founded 10 an Gearran 2669 BDE by the druids of Macha. Known for the druids who buried Muileann ghlas's dead.

A holy hill with a citadel south of the capital, the seat of Siorrachd Cnoc naomh and a house of the order of Macha since the Holy Age. It lies close by the battlefield of Muileann ghlas, and its druids buried the dead of both sides after the Long War's last battle. It is a large town of druids, soldiers and pilgrims.

  • 10 an t-Samhain 4707 BDE — Cnoc naomh
