Dùn fhiadhaich

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,664

Founded 20 an Giblean 1615 BDE by the lords of the wild hill. Known for refuge from the Great Wave.

A small wild city on a hill south of the capital, near Achadh mhin, which the Great Wave struck. Its hill kept it clear of the water, and it took in the survivors of the villages below. It follows the order of Macha. The clay of its hill makes it the largest pottery on Rodos, and Cathair fhada sells its ware to the north.

  • 4 an Lùnastal 1837 DE — Weighing the grain at Dùn fhiadhaich

Muileann ruadh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,657

Founded 14 an Lùnastal 1346 DE by red-sandstone millers. Known for red sandstone mill-house.

A small mill-town built of red sandstone, grinding for Baile chrom and the village of Cill fhada. It was never walled, relying on Baile chrom's walls in hard times. Its people keep the order of Macha, and the mill-house has a small shrine to Macha's black horse above the wheel.

Siorrachd Cnoc shean

Achadh fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,825

Founded 9 an t-Samhain 491 DE by farmers of Cnoc shean. Known for hay from the fair fields.

A fair field village in the south-east, with meadows between the hill-towns of Cnoc shean and Cnoc fhada. It keeps the Old Spirits and is known for its hay.

Àth dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,921

Founded 26 an Giblean 1801 DE by Ròdaich miners under extraction contract. Known for red ford of the mining camps.

Àth dhearg of Cnoc shean began as a mining camp at a ford in the Age of Strangers, and its red water is said to come from the spoil. It is neither the Àth dhearg whose name the northern lighthouse bears nor the western ford that the Great Hunger struck.

Cnoc fhada

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 9,834

Founded 18 am Màrt 1322 DE by hill-farmers of Cnoc shean. Known for terraced farms on the long hill.

A long hill in the south-east farmed in terraces since the centuries after the Sundering. It keeps the Old Spirits and trades with Muileann dhomhain.

Cnoc shean

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 21,362

Founded 18 am Màrt 2996 BDE by Ròdaich traders of the eastern plain. Known for old hill market of the granary fields.

Cnoc shean is the old hill market for the granary fields of Achadh mhòr, and the seat of its province. It is a town of more than twenty thousand, with grain-halls and a weighing-house older than any coinage on the island. The tavern An Sligeanach Fad' às lies on the road to Achadh mhòr, and its dried deer is sold in Cnoc shean's market.

  • 3 an Cèitean 1888 DE — The fever at Cnoc shean

Siorrachd Cnoc thais

Àth naomh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 12,892

Founded 26 an t-Sultain 219 BDE by Ròdaich druids of the holy ford; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for citadel over the holy ford.

The holy ford was a Ròdaich shrine and crossing, and a citadel was raised over it in the Holy Age. At the Severance the Ròdaich left and Tuathaich families took the town, which is now one of the largest they hold. They keep the citadel manned and the old shrine open as their church.

  • 6 an Giblean 2015 DE — Àth naomh joins the pit towns
  • 17 an Dùbhlachd 2020 DE — Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg

Baile shean

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,936

Founded 27 an Cèitean 2442 BDE by Ròdaich founders; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for old walls held by the Tuathaich.

An old Ròdaich town with walls and a citadel, emptied at the Severance and taken over by Tuathaich families. In the years before An Cogadh Fada it was counted among the northern communities that refused the dubhan economy. Its walls still stand, and the Tuathaich guard them as the Ròdaich once did.

Cnoc thais

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 19,291

Founded 13 an Giblean 67 BDE by Ròdaich hill-farmers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the market of the two ancient mills.

A damp hill in the north-west, seat of Siorrachd Cnoc thais, and one of the larger Tuathaich towns since the Severance. It follows the faith of the Church and is the market of the two Muileann àrsaidhs.

  • 19 an t-Sultain 3273 BDE — Cnoc thais in the north-west
  • 27 an t-Ògmhios 1870 DE — The masons of Cnoc thais
  • 7 am Màrt 1998 DE — Cnoc thais in the western hills
  • 4 an t-Samhain 2015 DE — Tom Varley's pits
  • 2 an Lùnastal 2020 DE — Cnoc thais taken

Muileann àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 4,008

Founded 20 an Giblean 1740 DE by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the younger ancient mill.

The younger of the two Muileann àrsaidhs, walled, a short distance from the elder. Gorta Baile chrom, the Great Hunger, struck it in the Age of Strangers, and it was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It follows the faith of the Church.

Siorrachd Cuan ghlas

Àth gharbh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,628

Founded 13 an Gearran 1477 DE by drovers of the central hills. Known for a drovers' ford in the hills.

A rough ford on the hill road near Baile Mòr uaine, where the drovers rest their beasts. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and is a very small place. Coinneachadh nan Cupan, the spring where the keeper's stone cup was first checked against its copies, lies on the moor between the ford and Tobar dhìreach.

  • 12 an Dàmhair 8440 BDE — The first small burning
  • 5 an Lùnastal 6590 BDE — The measured handful

Baile Mòr uaine

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,060

Founded 22 am Màrt 2017 BDE by custodians of Cuan ghlas. Known for walled city of the druid schools.

Baile Mòr uaine is a walled city with a citadel in the north-eastern hills, founded in the Holy Age. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and is among their strongholds. Its walls were repaired in the Age of Strangers. Its forges are the chief armoury of the north-eastern hills.

  • 15 an Dùbhlachd 1828 DE — The druid students of Baile Mòr uaine

Cill àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 9,277

Founded 29 an Cèitean 2326 BDE by teachers of the druid schools. Known for retreat of the druid teachers.

Cill àrsaidh of Cuan ghlas is an old cell that the teachers of Scoiltean nan Draoidhean, the druid schools, took as a retreat early in the schools' history. It became a large village of students and farmers. The schools' dormant teachers kept it alive through the Age of Strangers, and it filled again at the revival.

Cnoc chiar

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,643

Founded 24 am Faoilleach 2583 BDE by Ròdaich shepherds of Cuan ghlas. Known for sheep walks and wool market.

A large town on the dusky hill, living on the sheep walks above it and on the wool trade with Caol bheag. It was a mustering place for fleeces in the Age of Strangers, when the humans bought wool as eagerly as ore. Its market is the busiest in the province.

Cnoc thais

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,622

Founded 28 an Dùbhlachd 45 DE by shepherds of the Cuan ghlas hills. Known for mist, wool and hill cheese.

A damp hill-town above the river port of Cuan ghlas, its name taken from the mists that sit on it most mornings. It was never walled and never fought over, and its people send wool and cheese down to the river quays and to Cnoc chiar. A small house of the druid schools keeps the only books in the place.

Cuan ghlas

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 15,114

Founded 15 an t-Ògmhios 2778 BDE by grey-water fishers of the north-east. Known for the grey river port and its citadel.

A grey river port on the Abhainn ghorm in the north-east with a citadel, the seat of Siorrachd Cuan ghlas, and a large village, whose barges go down to Ros chiar at the river mouth. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and is served by the hill town of Cnoc thais above it.

Muileann bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 14,577

Founded 23 an t-Sultain 689 DE by millers of Cuan ghlas. Known for mills for Inis mhòr and Caol bheag.

Muileann bheag is a mill town of fourteen thousand grinding for Inis mhòr and Caol bheag. Its mills are among the busiest in the north. It is one of several places named Muileann bheag, and not the fort above the panther roads nor the town of the northern lighthouse.

Siorrachd Cuan ruadh

Baile ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,364

Founded 4 an Gearran 333 DE by Ròdaich slate-quarriers of Cuan ruadh. Known for grey slate of the east coast.

A small town of grey slate on the eastern coast, quarrying for the roofs of Achadh shean and Cnoc uaine. Its people keep the Old Spirits.

Cuan ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 19,209

Founded 1 an t-Sultain 477 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the east. Known for the island's easternmost harbour.

Cuan ruadh is the easternmost harbour of the island and the seat of its province, a port since the Holy Age. Its boats go out further than any on the coast, and it has lost more to pirates than any other eastern town. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Siorrachd Cuan shean

Àth naomh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,746

Founded 26 an Giblean 861 DE by druids of the order of Manannan. Known for blessing of the harbour carts.

A holy ford near Cuan shean, where the druids of Manannan bless the carts that go down to the harbour. It follows the order of Manannan and is a small town of shrine-keepers and carters. Bog-iron is dug in the moss behind the town, and its forges have made arms and field-guns for the regiments since An Cogadh Fada.

  • 20 an t-Ògmhios 2023 DE — The regiments' arms contracts

Baile ruadh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 17,942

Founded 9 am Màrt 1754 DE by red-clay potters of the Cuan shean country. Known for red roof-tiles and scorpion-marked jars.

A red town of potters and brick-makers behind the harbour of Cuan shean, whose kilns have fired the roof-tiles of the western coast since the centuries after the Sundering. It follows the order of Manannan, and its potters mark each jar with a small scorpion, the order's badge, under the base. Most of what it makes goes out through Cuan shean.

Cill thais

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,704

Founded 22 an Giblean 122 BDE by druids of the order of Manannan. Known for fortified shrine of Manannan over the fleet anchorage.

Cill thais is a shrine village on damp ground above the anchorage of Cuan shean, fortified with a citadel in the Holy Age to watch the western sea. The fourth fleet, raised in the Long War, is stationed at Cuan shean below, and the village's druids bless each ship in Manannan's name before it first puts out. It is a small place whose citadel is larger than its village.

Cuan shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 32,433

Founded 4 an Gearran 2627 BDE by the harbour-lords of the west coast. Known for the fourth fleet's harbour.

The old harbour of the west, the seat of Siorrachd Cuan shean and one of the largest towns on the island. It shipped western grain and timber through the Holy Age and served the human traders after the Crossing. Since the Long War it has been home to An ceathramh cabhlach, the fourth fleet. It follows the order of Manannan.

Doire gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,372

Founded 2 an Dàmhair 1304 BDE by Ròdaich shipwrights' woodwards. Known for rough oak for the western fleet.

A large walled village in rough oakwood that has supplied timber to the yards at Cuan shean since the Holy Age. When the fleet of Cuan shean was raised in the Long War its hulls were cut here. It follows the order of Manannan, as does most of the west.

Siorrachd Doire chaol

Àth fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,445

Founded 14 an t-Sultain 2004 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the capital. Known for wild ford on the capital's south road.

Àth fhiadhaich is the wild ford on the south road out of Cathair dhearg, a town of ten thousand that grew as the capital grew. Its crossing was paved in the Holy Age, and the road over it carries the capital's trade toward the southern coast. It follows the capital's order, the order of Macha, and its shrine keepers take part in the rites at Cathair dhearg.

  • 21 an Dàmhair 1998 BDE — The fight at Àth fhiadhaich

Doire chaol

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 24,225

Founded 30 an t-Sultain 1947 DE by households of the restored court. Known for the capital's household village.

Doire chaol was laid out after the Severance on a narrow oak strip by the Abhainn dhomhain south of the capital, to house the families of the royal household. It grew into a large village, and in the kingdom's fourth decade it was cut out of the shire of Baile chiar as a shire of its own, the only shire made since the drawing. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

  • 20 an Giblean 1814 DE — The carters of Doire chaol

Siorrachd Doire chiar

Cill dhearg

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,761

Founded 7 an t-Samhain 2450 BDE by druids of the schools. Known for red temple-house by the old bridge.

A temple village of red stone near Drochaid Ros fhionn, whose house of the druid schools gave shelter to travellers crossing the old bridge when the river trade was busy. As the trade dried up and the bridge fell out of use, the village shrank to its temple-house and a few farms. Its druids still keep a lamp at the bridge-end.

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,684

Founded 7 an t-Samhain 1222 DE by flax-growers of the north. Known for flax fields and linen.

Cnoc ìseal, the low hill, is a small town of the north-east given to flax and linen. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and has changed little since. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Doire chiar

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 23,587

Founded 28 am Faoilleach 1575 BDE by oak-keepers of the north-east. Known for disputations under the oaks.

A dusky oak grove grown into a large village, the seat of Siorrachd Doire chiar. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith, and its druids are said to hold their disputations under the oldest trees.

  • 8 an Giblean 3418 BDE — Doire chiar
  • 23 an t-Ògmhios 445 DE — Eilidh Dhubh's tracts
  • 30 an Giblean 1869 DE — The last disputation at Doire chiar

Muileann fhada

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,677

Founded 10 am Màrt 746 DE by millers of Doire chiar. Known for flour for Doire chiar.

A long mill in the north-east beside Muileann dhearg, grinding for the large village of Doire chiar. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Siorrachd Doire fhada

Cuan uaine

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,529

Founded 23 an Dùbhlachd 465 BDE by Ròdaich custodians of the capital's east. Known for the temple of Macha on the Abhainn fhionn.

Cuan uaine, whose name means the green harbour, is a walled temple city on the Abhainn fhionn east of the capital, fortified in the Holy Age to guard the river road to the eastern shore. Its temple of Macha is much visited by those who cannot reach the capital's. The barracks town of Inis mhòr lies just upriver to the north. Its copyists and tailors work for the capital.

  • 5 an t-Sultain 1929 DE — Cuan uaine opens its quays

Doire fhada

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 21,905

Founded 27 am Faoilleach 986 BDE by oak-cutters of the capital's forests. Known for ship-timber and the fenced oak.

A long oak grove east of the capital cut for ship-timber since the Holy Age, and the shipwrights who built the Sundering fleet are said to have taken their keels here. The village grew enormous without changing its name, and it is now the seat of Siorrachd Doire fhada and a river port of the capital's order, Macha's, on the Abhainn fhionn. The grove itself is mostly gone, and the village keeps one old oak fenced by the river quay.

Siorrachd Doire fhiadhaich

Cnoc shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,179

Founded 6 an t-Sultain 1782 BDE by Ròdaich herders of the south. Known for market common on the old hill.

Cnoc shean, the old hill, is a small town of the south, settled since the Holy Age. Its common holds the market of the farms around it. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Doire fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 27,501

Founded 19 an Lùnastal 1018 BDE by the oak-keepers of the south. Known for timber for Cathair fhada.

A wild oak grove in the south, grown into a very large village and the seat of Siorrachd Doire fhiadhaich. It follows the order of Macha and supplies timber to the city of Cathair fhada close by.

  • 15 an Dàmhair 1810 DE — Meal-carts at Doire fhiadhaich

Siorrachd Doire fhionn

Achadh àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,452

Founded 12 an t-Ògmhios 2178 BDE by Ròdaich herders on an older field. Known for field-walls older than any record.

Achadh àrsaidh, the ancient field, was named by Ròdaich herders who found its field-walls already standing and old when they came. No record says who laid them. Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, struck it in the Age of Strangers and parched its hay-meadows for three dry seasons running. It has stayed a small village of cattle and hay on the eastern uplands, keeping the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and its walls in repair.

Àth ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,509

Founded 25 an t-Sultain 664 BDE by cattle-drovers of the eastern hills. Known for the drovers' ford and cattle fair.

A red-banked ford where the drovers' road crosses a stream in the east, it has been a cattle-market since the Holy Age. It keeps the Old Spirits of the Ròdaich, and the drovers still pour a cup into the ford before driving a herd across. The town trades beasts to Seann Dunn on the coast and hides to Baile shean. Furs and hides from the eastern hills are sold at its fair.

Àth uaine

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,572

Founded 25 an Giblean 1676 DE by the wardens of the Achadh shean road. Known for garrisoned green ford.

A small garrison town at the green ford on the road between Doire fhionn and Achadh shean. Its citadel is larger than the town needs, a sign that the ford was once contested, though the record does not preserve by whom. Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, struck it in the Age of Strangers, and it lives now on toll and on the soldiers who still keep the tower.

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 9,699

Founded 1 an t-Samhain 212 DE by carters of the Seann Dunn road. Known for straight road to Seann Dunn.

A town of one straight road running down to Seann Dunn, whose carters take the dyed cloth of Baile ghorm to the harbour. It is a town of nearly ten thousand. It keeps the Old Spirits.

Baile ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 4,277

Founded 22 an Lùnastal 270 DE by Ròdaich dyers from Achadh shean. Known for woad dyers and blue-washed houses.

Baile ghorm grew up around woad pits and dye-houses, and in the chroniclers' day its houses were still washed blue from the vats. It sent cloth to Seann Dunn for shipping and yarn to Achadh shean for weaving. The Old Spirits, the folk tradition of the ancestors, hold here strongly, and the dyers still leave a first skein at the hearth-stone each season.

Baile shean

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,687

Founded 5 an Dàmhair 1344 BDE by keepers of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar. Known for the keepers of the sacred forest's edge.

An old town beside Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, the forest marked sacred before any faith claimed it. Its people have kept the forest's edge since the Holy Age and keep the Old Spirits, though the forest is now held by the druid schools.

Cill àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,982

Founded 19 an Giblean 551 BDE by keepers of the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. Known for ancient cell of the ancestor rite.

Cill àrsaidh of the north is an old cell of the ancestor rite, founded in the Holy Age and never much more than a village around its shrine. It lies inland of the Hawk bay and has kept to the Old Spirits while its neighbours took up the Hawk order and the rite of Mòd. The shrine keepers are hereditary. Its people gather amber on the strands of the Hawk bay.

Cnoc ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 8,412

Founded 22 an Dàmhair 2265 BDE by bee-keepers of the north. Known for blue hill and bee-keeping.

Cnoc ghorm of Doire fhionn is a town of the north-central country, founded in the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and its bees, whose wax lit the shrines at Cill àrsaidh before dubhan lamps came.

Doire fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 21,604

Founded 20 am Màrt 2602 BDE by Ròdaich woodsmen of the east. Known for great oak grove of the east.

Doire fhionn of the east is the seat of its province, a great village of the Holy Age in an oak grove, which has never been raised to the rank of town despite its size. Its oaks are managed under rules older than the kingdom. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits, and the old field-village of Achadh àrsaidh lies to its north.

  • 10 an Gearran 9224 BDE — The deer-drives of the eastern forest
  • 5 an Dàmhair 1886 DE — Doire fhionn walks for water

Doire fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 13,873

Founded 4 an t-Samhain 1850 BDE by the oak-keepers of the Old Spirits. Known for an uncut grove of the ancestors.

A fair oak grove in the north, the seat of Siorrachd Doire fhionn and a large village of the Old Spirits. The grove has never been cut for ship-timber, its keepers holding it for the ancestors, and it lies on the road between Cathair naomh and the Tuathaich line.

  • 26 an Lùnastal 35 BDE — The oaks of Doire fhionn

Muileann ruadh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,120

Founded 29 an Giblean 1416 BDE by Ròdaich millers of the north. Known for red mill and border citadel.

Muileann ruadh of Doire fhionn is a mill town of the north-central country, founded in the Holy Age. Its citadel was raised after the Severance to watch the Tuathaich border. It keeps the Hawk order of the Old Faith.

Tobar ghorm

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,465

Founded 27 am Faoilleach 78 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers of the northern road. Known for blue spring on the northern road.

A village around a blue spring on the road running north toward the Tuathaich country, and the last Ròdaich water on that road. Since the Severance it has traded with both sides of the line and has been trusted by neither. It is not the larger Tobar ghorm of the wool fairs, and it resents the confusion.

Siorrachd Doire ghlas

Cnoc mhòr

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 5,564

Founded 5 an t-Sultain 1194 DE by Ròdaich herders; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for keepers of the Muileann bheag light.

Cnoc mhòr of Doire ghlas is a Tuathaich town of the north coast, founded by Ròdaich herders in the long quiet centuries and resettled after the Severance. Its people supply the keepers of Taigh-solais Muileann bheag. It keeps the faith of the Church.

  • 17 an Lùnastal 1876 DE — Cnoc mhòr walks south

Doire fhionn

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 5,264

Founded 5 an Dàmhair 443 DE by Ròdaich woodwards; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for pale oaks and Tuathaich hearth-tellings.

A Ròdaich village in a grove of pale oaks, left empty at the Severance and resettled by Tuathaich families sent north. Its people keep the Tuathaich Church, and it is one of the northern households where the voyage of Naomh Breandan is still told at the hearth, a telling the Ròdaich druids call superstition. It lives on timber and on the fort at Cnoc leathan nearby.

Doire ghlas

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 40,740

Founded 7 an t-Iuchar 1266 DE by Ròdaich oak-cutters, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the great Tuathaich gathering-village.

A small Ròdaich village in a grey oak grove until the Severance, when the families shepherded north were gathered here before being sent on, and so many stayed that it became the largest settlement in the Tuathaich homeland almost at once. It never took a town's name, and the Tuathaich keep it a village in speech on purpose. It is the seat of Siorrachd Doire ghlas and the heart of the Tuathaich Church, whose priests are said to hold the oldest copy of the voyage of Naomh Breandan here; the library has asked to copy it and been refused. Its wool mills, built with the Moot's money, make the grey twill of the north.

Siorrachd Doire mhin

Baile bhàn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 9,453

Founded 19 an Dùbhlachd 1199 DE by Ròdaich traders of Doire mhin. Known for white town on the Muileann ghlas road.

Baile bhàn is a white town of nine thousand near Cathair mhòr, on the road toward Muileann ghlas. Before the last battle of the Long War the state's columns marched through it. It follows the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Baile chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,296

Founded 24 am Faoilleach 231 DE by the tithe-reeves of Cathair mhòr. Known for the walled tithe-granaries.

A walled town on a bend of the road below Cathair mhòr, raised to store and guard the tithe-grain of the Doire mhin country. Its walls were strengthened when the human administration raised the tithe, and the chroniclers note that the grain was guarded but not shared. It keeps the order of Macha and serves Cill fhada and Muileann ruadh as their market. The dubhan works under its walls supply the forges of the gulf, and the town boils soap.

  • 11 an Gearran 1853 DE — The Green Death at Baile chrom

Cathair mhòr

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,637

Founded 28 an Cèitean 852 BDE by the lords of Doire mhin. Known for the citadel on the capital's north road.

A hill-city with a citadel close to the capital, raised by lords of the Doire mhin country who held the roads north of Cathair dhearg. It has always been a garrison town and was one of the strongholds from which the war before the Severance was fought. It follows the order of Macha and draws on the tithe-granaries of Baile chrom and the great village of Doire mhin. It is not the Cathair mhòr of the third regiment, which lies further east. Its glass-house is the largest on the island.

Cnoc chiar

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,716

Founded 10 an t-Samhain 1564 DE by herders of Doire mhin. Known for hill pastures of Doire mhin.

A small dusky hill between Doire mhin and Muileann ruadh, pastured by herders of the great village. It follows the order of Macha.

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,411

Founded 31 an Cèitean 4 DE by farmers of Doire mhin. Known for hill farms by Muileann ghlas field.

Cnoc ìseal of Doire mhin is a small town of hill farms east of the capital, founded in the long quiet centuries. The field of Muileann ghlas, where An Cogadh Fada ended, lies just to the west, and the town's barns sheltered the wounded after the battle. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Doire mhin

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 33,558

Founded 10 an t-Ògmhios 739 BDE by the oak-keepers of the capital's north. Known for the great grove-village of the north road.

A smooth-barked oak grove north of the capital, grown into one of the largest settlements on the island while keeping its village name and customs. It is the seat of Siorrachd Doire mhin and follows the order of Macha. Its people farm for Cathair mhòr and send much of their grain to the tithe-granaries at Baile chrom.

  • 18 an Dàmhair 356 BDE — The bridge at Doire mhin
  • 24 an t-Sultain 516 DE — The burning of Doire mhin
  • 31 an Dùbhlachd 1800 DE — The last count at Doire mhin

Siorrachd Doire shean

Àth gharbh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,556

Founded 28 an t-Sultain 1144 BDE by drovers of the western road. Known for the First Fleet's walled ford town.

Àth gharbh, the rough ford, is a walled town of the south-west, a short walk from Doire shean and its great roadside tavern, Am Buabhall Fortanach. That tavern fortified with the others of the old mining circuit before the war of the Severance. Since An Cogadh Fada, A' chiad chabhlach has been stationed here and carries the town's name; its hulls lie in the harbour of Doire shean below.

  • 13 an Cèitean 2020 DE — A' chiad chabhlach raised

Doire shean

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 35,064

Founded 14 an Lùnastal 1810 BDE by the tavern-keepers of the south-west. Known for Am Buabhall Fortanach and jugged buffalo.

An old oak grove in the south-west, grown into one of the largest villages on the island and the seat of Siorrachd Doire shean. At its heart is Am Buabhall Fortanach, the most famous tavern on the old roads, which serves jugged buffalo and has stood since the Holy Age. It is a harbour as well, where the hulls of the first fleet of Àth gharbh lie, and follows the order of the Stone. Rathad na Banrighinn, Queen Catrìona's stone road from the capital to Inis thais, runs through the village past the tavern.

  • 24 an t-Ògmhios 1959 DE — Doire shean's harbour

Siorrachd Dùn chrom

Àth dhubh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,063

Founded 1 an t-Sultain 738 DE by Ròdaich ferrymen of Dùn chrom. Known for the black ford and its walls.

The black ford takes its name from the dark water over the crossing. Walls were raised in the Age of Strangers, when the crossing carried much of the capital's traffic eastward. The Battle of Muileann ghlas, the last of An Cogadh Fada, was fought within sight of its walls.

Àth mhin

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,630

Founded 7 an t-Ògmhios 1025 DE by wardens of the Dùn chrom crossings. Known for the smooth ford and its citadel.

A walled town with a citadel at the smooth ford, one of a chain of crossings east of the capital. It was a quartering place for soldiers in the Age of Strangers and again in the Long War, when it held the state's stores for the campaign that ended at Muileann ghlas. Its people are mostly carters and stable-keepers.

Baile chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,068

Founded 5 am Màrt 643 DE by herders from Dùn chrom. Known for Dùn chrom's stockyards.

The lesser of the two Baile chroms in the central midlands, this one lies under the citadel of Dùn chrom and grew as its stockyard. The fighting at Muileann ghlas in the last year of the Long War passed close enough that the town housed wounded for a season. It keeps the order of Macha.

Cnoc leathan

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,626

Founded 12 an Dàmhair 1150 DE by Ròdaich herders of Dùn chrom. Known for lodgings and horse-lines for Fèill Muileann òg.

A modest town on the broad hill beside Muileann òg, whose people live for most of the year on herding and for one season on the fair. Since Fèill Muileann òg became the island's greatest gathering, Cnoc leathan has lodged the traders the fair town cannot hold and stabled their animals. It stood near the lines at Muileann ghlas and was emptied for the battle.

Dùn chrom

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 21,065

Founded 27 an t-Sultain 707 BDE by the lords of the bent hill. Known for the citadel above Muileann ghlas.

A fortified city on a crooked hill in the midlands, seat of Siorrachd Dùn chrom, with a citadel that commands the roads south of the capital. The last battle of the Long War, at Muileann ghlas, was fought within sight of its citadel, and the crown's commanders used its citadel as their headquarters. It follows the order of Macha and is served by the stockyard town of Baile chrom and the ford at Àth mhin.

Muileann ghlas

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,877

Founded 16 an t-Samhain 2251 BDE by Ròdaich millers of Dùn chrom. Known for the last battle of the Long War.

The grey mill is an old grain town near the fair at Muileann òg and within a day of the capital. It is remembered above all for the Battle of Muileann ghlas, the second and final major battle of An Cogadh Fada, fought on its fields, in which the Tuathaich holdouts were broken. The battlefield, Àraich Muileann ghlas, lies just north-west of the town.

  • 6 an Dùbhlachd 2021 DE — The camp by Muileann ghlas

Muileann òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,667

Founded 10 am Faoilleach 1950 DE by millers of the restored kingdom. Known for Fèill Muileann òg, the great fair.

Muileann òg, the young mill, was built in the first years of the restored kingdom. Its annual fair, Fèill Muileann òg, became the island's largest gathering. The field of Muileann ghlas, where An Cogadh Fada ended, lies close by. Rathad na Fèille, the fair road, was metalled from Cathair dhearg in the fair's first years.

  • 13 an Giblean 2000 BDE — The War of the Roads begins at Muileann òg
  • 20 an Giblean 1910 DE — The old market at Muileann òg

Siorrachd Dùn dhearg

Àth àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,029

Founded 19 am Màrt 1105 BDE by the ford-keepers of Dùn dhearg. Known for the pebble-cairn at the ford-stone.

An ancient ford in the east, between the mill town of Muileann leathan and Seann Mhorn on the coast. It keeps the Old Spirits and a ford-stone where travellers leave a pebble, and it has been a small crossing town since the Holy Age.

Cill bhàn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,569

Founded 20 am Màrt 2723 BDE by keepers of the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. Known for white cell of the ancestor rite.

Cill bhàn, the white cell, is a village of the Old Spirits' ancestor rite in the east, founded in the Holy Age. It lies near the hot springs and the silver workings of the vein country. It has kept its spirit-house through every age and every change of master.

Cnoc ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,914

Founded 21 an Dùbhlachd 655 DE by quarriers for Dùn dhearg. Known for grey stone for Dùn dhearg.

Cnoc ghlas is the grey hill whose stone built much of Dùn dhearg. It is a quarry town, dependent on the city. Its quarrymen keep the Old Spirits' rites of the ancestors and will not open a new face without them.

  • 22 an Dàmhair 2972 BDE — The weather-cairns of Cnoc ghlas
  • 13 an Giblean 527 BDE — The late snow on the high passes

Dùn dhearg

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 25,678

Founded 27 an Giblean 2914 BDE by a custodian house of the eastern hills. Known for red hill-fort city of the east.

Dùn dhearg is the red hill-fort city of the east and the seat of its province, a city of more than twenty-five thousand. The mills of Muileann dhomhain grind its bread and the quarries of Cnoc ghlas built its houses. It keeps the Old Spirits, and its old fort is the site of the province's ancestor feasts.

Muileann gheal

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 12,710

Founded 7 an Dàmhair 1043 DE by white-stone millers. Known for flour for Dùn dhearg.

A white stone mill in the south-east that grinds for the city of Dùn dhearg. It keeps the Old Spirits and is a large mill-town with a guild of millers older than the city's walls.

  • 26 an Lùnastal 1400 DE — The grey glaze of Muileann gheal
  • 30 an Dùbhlachd 1470 DE — The grey glaze lost

Tobar ìseal

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,174

Founded 26 am Faoilleach 469 DE by well-keepers of Dùn dhearg. Known for the well that waters Dùn dhearg.

A low well-village in the east that waters the city of Dùn dhearg in dry seasons. It keeps the Old Spirits, and its well-keepers still bless the water before it is carted up the hill.

Siorrachd Dùn ìseal

Baile naomh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,008

Founded 1 an Gearran 2680 BDE by custodians of the holy wells. Known for holy wells of the vein country.

Baile naomh, the holy town, grew around wells in the vein country that the Holy Age custodians held sacred. The hot springs of Muileann ruadh lie to the west and the silver workings of Muileann chiar to the north-west. It is a small town of shrines and lodging houses, keeping the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Cill dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,922

Founded 6 am Màrt 349 BDE by druids of the schools for the silver-miners. Known for miners' temple by the silver seam.

A temple village a short way from the silver seam at Muileann chiar, whose house of the druid schools has served the silver-miners since the seam was first worked. In the Age of Strangers its druids kept a record of the miners killed underground, one of the few such records to survive. It is not the Cill dhìreach of the central country.

Cnoc àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,625

Founded 5 an t-Sultain 2222 BDE by shepherds of the eastern hills. Known for cairn hill and its shepherds.

Cnoc àrsaidh of Dùn ìseal is a hill town crowned by old cairns, above Baile naomh. It has been a shepherding place since the Holy Age. Its people keep the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and tend the cairns at the turning of the seasons.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 9,720

Founded 7 an t-Iuchar 1859 DE by silver miners of Muileann chiar. Known for the citadel over the silver seam.

A young hill-town with a citadel beside the silver mine of Muileann chiar, raised when the Ròdaich held the silver seam against the human claims. The citadel was built to guard the seam, and the town grew as the silver town expanded. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Dùn ìseal

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 22,571

Founded 10 an Dàmhair 2997 BDE by the custodian house of Dùn ìseal. Known for the Hall of Brìde's flame.

A low fort-city in the east with walls, a citadel and a temple, the seat of Siorrachd Dùn ìseal. Its temple is the Hall where Brìde's undying flame was first bound, kept by the Ròdaich custodians through every age; the townsfolk themselves keep the Old Spirits, and their ancestor hall beside it is the chief spirit-house of the eastern hills. It stands between the silver seam of Muileann chiar and the hot springs of Muileann ruadh, and it was held by the Ròdaich in the dispute over the silver. It is the market town of the eastern hills and plain, and the market under the Hall is older than the kingdom. The silver, gold and copper of its hills pass through it as blanks for the mint, and the town salts venison and binds books.

Muileann chiar

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,771

Founded 10 an Lùnastal 2992 BDE by Ròdaich custodians who found the silver seam. Known for the island's silver seam.

Muileann chiar was founded when a silver seam was found near, but distinct from, the great vein, the island's first confirmed resource that was not obsidian. In the Age of Strangers human interests tried to claim the silver as well, and the Ròdaich kept it; the town grew alongside the obsidian workings as demand for both rose. It is smaller now than in its great years.

Muileann dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 8,100

Founded 23 am Màrt 362 BDE by Ròdaich millers of Dùn ìseal. Known for its deep-cut mill-race.

The deep mill takes its name from a mill-race cut far down into the rock to reach a steady flow. It grinds for Dùn dhearg and the villages around it and has done so since the Holy Age. The Old Spirits, the folk tradition of the ancestors, hold here, and each new millstone is blessed at the hearth before it is set.

Muileann ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,558

Founded 11 an t-Ògmhios 2594 BDE by keepers of the hot springs. Known for the hot springs of Muileann ruadh.

A red walled mill town beside Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh, the hot springs whose warm water drives its wheel through winter. The springs were held sacred by the Old Spirits, and the healers of the Old Faith call them Dian Cècht's, and the town walled them against claims from the human administration. It is a place for the sick and the old to bathe.

Siorrachd Dùn thais

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,837

Founded 12 an Lùnastal 1362 DE by carters of Dùn thais. Known for narrow ford on the Dùn thais road.

A small town at a narrow ford on the Dùn thais road, living on the carts that pass through it. Since the library was founded at Muileann chaol many of its young people have gone to work there as porters and copyists. It has never been walled or fought over.

Àth dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,388

Founded 6 an t-Ògmhios 1069 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of Dùn thais. Known for deep ford below Muileann chaol.

The deep ford lies below Muileann chaol, and every reader bound for the library crosses it. It is a town of eleven thousand. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Baile leathan

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,418

Founded 21 am Faoilleach 906 BDE by Ròdaich scribes of Dùn thais. Known for copyists and binders for the library.

Baile leathan is one of the towns nearest Leabharlann Muileann chaol, and many of its people are copyists, binders and parchment-makers for the library. It was a market town of the broad valley long before the library was founded, and it grew quickly after. It keeps the druid schools' habit of reading aloud in the evenings.

Dùn thais

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 34,173

Founded 20 am Màrt 2469 BDE by custodians of the north-eastern hills. Known for great hill city near the Library.

Dùn thais of the north-east is a great hill city with a citadel and a temple, the chief place of its province. It lies close to Leabharlann Muileann chaol, and many of the Library's clerks and copyists live in it. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith, and its temple is sacred to Flidais, lady of the deer. Its tailors and smiths work for the library's clerks and the hill towns, and its own woods give timber.

Muileann àrsaidh

fort · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,831

Founded 19 am Faoilleach 1329 BDE by a custodian house of Dùn thais. Known for fortified ancient mill.

Muileann àrsaidh is an ancient mill fortified with a citadel, a short way from Muileann chaol. The citadel guarded the road to the ore in the Holy Age and now guards the road to the library. It is a small place of fewer than two thousand.

Siorrachd Inis bhàn

Doire ruadh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,987

Founded 24 an Cèitean 1452 DE by hawk-keepers of the north. Known for red oak grove and hawk-keepers.

Doire ruadh is a village of red oaks inland of the Hawk bay, founded in the long quiet centuries by families who kept hawks for the rite of Mòd, the hungry hawk of Acaill. Its birds are still flown at the Hawk order's gatherings in Cnoc bheag. Since the Severance it has lain close to the Tuathaich border and has seen more soldiers than it wishes.

Inis bhàn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 37,990

Founded 16 an Giblean 2587 BDE by Ròdaich boatmen of the white island. Known for white-island river port and Hawk-order shrines.

Inis bhàn is the great river port of the north-west Ròdaich country and the seat of its province, a town of nearly forty thousand on the Abhainn ìseal whose barges run down to Ros gheal on the coast. It is a town of the Hawk order, and its shrines face down the river toward the sea. The Green Death, A' Phlàigh Uaine, struck it in the Age of Strangers. It is one of several towns that claim the dock from which the ships of the Sundering set out, a claim the others dispute and no roll can settle.

Achadh gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 9,900

Founded 7 an Dàmhair 166 DE by farmers from Inis bheag. Known for stony fields that feed Inis bheag.

Rough ground behind the river port of Inis bheag, broken to the plough in the long centuries after the Sundering fleet had gone. It feeds the river port and its fishing boats, and it has grown larger than many towns while keeping the name and customs of a village. The druid schools have a strong following among its farmers, who are said to argue the schools' questions over the furrow.

Achadh gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,679

Founded 3 am Faoilleach 1065 DE by farmers of Muileann chaol. Known for stony fields for the old mill.

A rough field village beside the older Muileann chaol, breaking stony ground for the mill. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and shares its name with two other Achadh gharbhs of the east, which the library's clerks tell apart only by their shires.

Inis bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 21,240

Founded 25 an t-Iuchar 1564 BDE by boat-builders of the north-east. Known for boatyards of the small isle.

Inis bheag is an island town on the Abhainn bheag in the north-east and the seat of its province. Its boatyards have built fishing craft for the coast since the Holy Age and send them down the river to the sea at Caol chrom. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and shares its river with Ros fhionn of the old bridge.

  • 29 an Dàmhair 1832 DE — Ore through Inis bheag

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,708

Founded 15 an Giblean 1527 DE by red-stone millers. Known for red mill beside Muileann fhada.

A red mill town beside Muileann fhada in the north-east, the two together grinding for Doire chiar. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Ros fhionn

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,812

Founded 29 an Lùnastal 2958 BDE by custodians of the river crossing. Known for Drochaid Ros fhionn, the old bridge.

Ros fhionn of Inis bheag is a walled city on a headland over the Abhainn bheag, founded in the Holy Age where the first bridges crossed the river. Drochaid Ros fhionn, the old crossing, is still standing. It has seen little traffic since the salt went by sea, except for the century when the Company's ore carts crossed it on the eastern ore road, and it fell silent again when the eastern pits flooded in the Severance war. The salt-boats' lane round the east cape, Seòlaid Ros fhionn, is named for the town. Its temple is a hall of the druid schools, sacred to Flidais. The salt trade that built the bridge has gone, but the market-court the salt-masters set up stayed on the headland, and the town is still the market of fifty-three towns of the north-eastern hills, the widest reach of any market. Its yards on the river build barges and hulls, and it makes cheese for the hill towns.

Tobar òg

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,303

Founded 21 an t-Iuchar 1356 DE by well-diggers of Inis bheag. Known for the young well behind Inis bheag.

A young well village in the north-east, dug to water the fields behind Inis bheag when those fields were first broken. It has grown into a sizeable village and follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Siorrachd Inis chrom

Baile shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,839

Founded 18 an t-Iuchar 1814 BDE by Ròdaich followers of the order of the Stone. Known for old walled town of the order of the Stone.

An old walled town of Òrd na Cloiche, the order of the Stone, beside the fort of Muileann bheag. Its walls are older than the fort, and for most of its history it was the stronger of the two. It is small now, and lives on the fort's custom.

Cnoc shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,784

Founded 19 an Dùbhlachd 2797 BDE by the lords of the old hill. Known for the old hill citadel.

A small old hill-town with a citadel in the west, commanding the road between Baile Mòr fhionn and the harbours of the south-west. It follows the order of the Stone and has kept a garrison since the war before the Severance.

Inis chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 31,994

Founded 25 an Giblean 1398 BDE by sailors of the Stone's order from the south-west. Known for bent isle harbour and its sailors of the Stone.

Inis chrom is a large walled harbour on a bent island in the mouth of the Abhainn ghorm in the south-west. It has been a port since the Holy Age and its sailors keep the order of the Stone. It lies close to Am Buabhall Fortanach and Àth gharbh.

Baile ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 11,186

Founded 9 an t-Iuchar 2042 BDE by Ròdaich farmers of the red ground. Known for a shared market on the border.

A red town in the north-west that stayed Ròdaich when the Tuathaich homeland was fixed around it, and the line of the border wall that was proposed and never built would have run past its gate. It keeps the Old Spirits of the Ròdaich, and its market is used by Tuathaich from Baile fhionn and Ròdaich from Àth uaine alike.

Inis mhin

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 12,779

Founded 17 an Gearran 1152 DE by Ròdaich harbour-folk; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for Tuathaich port where Naomh Breandan's voyage is told.

Inis mhin was a Ròdaich harbour of the long quiet centuries on a tidal islet of the north coast, and its citadel was raised in the Age of Strangers by human administrators guarding the northern landing. After the Severance it passed wholly to the Tuathaich, and it is now one of their chief ports. It is among the coastal towns where the voyage of Naomh Breandan is still told, and its church keeps the old Tuathaich telling more closely than the churches of its neighbours. In the first spring of the Severance war the Leaden Hawk company, Buidheann an t-Seabhaig Luaidhe, lay twelve hours in the town and heard of the constables riding the western roads.

Siorrachd Inis mhòr

Cnoc naomh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 7,832

Founded 29 an Cèitean 1857 BDE by a custodian house of Inis mhòr. Known for citadel on the holy hill.

The holy hill carried a shrine before it carried a citadel; the citadel was added to guard Inis mhòr from the hills. The shrine still stands inside the walls. The fourth regiment from Caol bheag drills on the plain below it. On the moor above the town is Coinneachadh a' Mhonaidh, the cairn where the crew-leaders of the northern pits fixed the week of their rising.

Inis mhòr

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 23,990

Founded 31 an Lùnastal 2037 BDE by net-fishers of the Abhainn ghorm. Known for north-eastern river fleet and debating halls.

Inis mhòr of the north-east is the great river port of its province, on the Abhainn ghorm, a fishing town of the Holy Age that became a city under the Age of Strangers' trade; its barges run down the river to Ros chiar at the mouth. Its people follow the druid schools of the Old Faith, and the town's debating halls were among the first to reopen at the schools' revival. It shares the river and coastal trade with Ceann bheag and the walled town of Baile Mòr dhìreach inland.

Siorrachd Inis thais

Àth ghlas

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 16,521

Founded 31 am Faoilleach 1586 BDE by Ròdaich traders of Inis thais. Known for grey ford market of the west.

Àth ghlas is a large ford-market of the west, near Seann Warr. It follows the order of Manannan. It is one of three places named Àth ghlas and the largest.

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,014

Founded 14 an t-Iuchar 1353 DE by traders of the order of Manannan from the west. Known for straight-street harbour of the order of Manannan.

Baile dhìreach, the straight town, is a harbour on the west coast built around one long street to the quay. It was founded in the long quiet centuries by traders of the order of Manannan, among neighbours of the order of the Stone. The two orders have shared its market without any trouble the rolls think worth noting.

Caol fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,425

Founded 13 an t-Iuchar 700 DE by fishers of the wild strait. Known for fishing the wild strait.

Caol fhiadhaich is a harbour on a rough strait of the west coast, within the province of Inis thais. It was founded in the long quiet centuries by fishers who braved waters the older harbours avoided. Its people keep the Old Faith in the order of the Stone. Its women distil scent-waters, the town's second trade after the fishing. The southern sea-lane, Slighe-mhara Caol fhiadhaich, is named for its fishers, who first sailed it round the south coast in the long quiet centuries.

Inis thais

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 34,904

Founded 21 an Lùnastal 2656 BDE by druids of the order of the Stone. Known for the temple of Lia Fàil and its pilgrims.

Inis thais is a walled temple city of the south-west and the seat of its province. Its temple of Lia Fàil, the stone called Clach that cries out under the rightful king, is the chief house of the order of the Stone, and pilgrims come to it from Caol leathan and the whole western coast. It has been a holy city since the Holy Age. Besides its pilgrims it lives on its shipyard, which builds seagoing hulls for the western coast, and on its cheese and books. Buidheann an t-Seabhaig Luaidhe, the Leaden Hawk company sent by the council in the Severance war, ended its road at the temple here; the druids of Lia Fàil kept the city out of the war but shut its harbour to the Company's ships.

Siorrachd Muileann àrsaidh

Achadh àrsaidh

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,756

Founded 14 am Màrt 2396 BDE by Ròdaich fishers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the watch for the Sea-Watcher.

An ancient field village on the far western coast, facing the waters of Uilebheist na Mara, the Sea-Watcher. Gorta Baile chrom, the Great Hunger, struck it in the Age of Strangers; it was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance and keeps the faith of the Church. Pirates have been seen offshore and the villagers keep watch on the headland. Its boats first met the humans' ships at sea, off the north-west cape at the place they call Coinneachadh nan Long.

Achadh fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,753

Founded 19 an t-Iuchar 1473 DE by Ròdaich fishers of the west coast. Known for fishing within sight of the Sea-Watcher's waters.

A wild field village on the far western shore with a small harbour, kept in Ròdaich hands when the Tuathaich homeland was fixed to the north. It faces the waters where the Sea-Watcher is said to live, and pirates are still seen off the coast. Its people follow the order of Manannan.

Cathair gheal

city · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 9,818

Founded 5 am Màrt 1813 BDE by Ròdaich builders; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for white walls against the pirate coast.

Cathair gheal is a walled city of white stone on the far western coast, built by the Ròdaich and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its walls face the sea, where pirate ships have been seen offshore. It is the market for the Tuathaich villages of Muileann àrsaidh province. Its smiths make the tools of the north-west.

  • 8 an Giblean 1949 DE — Cathair gheal arms its boats

Cnoc bhàn

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 6,480

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd 23 DE by Ròdaich fishers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for harbour facing the pirate waters.

Cnoc bhàn of the north-west is a harbour facing the pirate waters. It was founded by Ròdaich fishers in the long quiet centuries and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its boats avoid the waters where old sailors place the Sea-Watcher.

Cnoc gheal

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,883

Founded 16 an Cèitean 516 DE by Ròdaich shepherds; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for white hill sheepfolds on the line.

A white hill of sheepfolds, Ròdaich until the Severance and Tuathaich since. The Ròdaich Cnoc gheal lies a short walk south-west, over the line. The two villages share a name and very little else: the one has its church, the other its shrine of Manannan.

Cnoc uaine

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 6,864

Founded 9 an Dàmhair 899 DE by Ròdaich herders; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for green hill grazing.

Cnoc uaine of Muileann àrsaidh is a green hill of the north-west, founded by Ròdaich herders in the long quiet centuries. It was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is a grazing town and keeps the faith of the Church.

Muileann àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,643

Founded 10 an t-Iuchar 555 BDE by Ròdaich millers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the old mill of the north-west.

Muileann àrsaidh, the ancient mill, is the younger of the two Muileann àrsaidh in the Tuathaich north-west, founded as a Ròdaich mill town in the Holy Age; the seat of the shire is the elder town close by. It was walled in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. The mill still grinds for the surrounding villages.

  • 28 an Cèitean 1929 DE — Muileann àrsaidh closes its road

Muileann àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 12,968

Founded 2 an Gearran 621 BDE by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the elder of the two ancient mills.

An ancient mill town of the north-west, and seat of Siorrachd Muileann àrsaidh, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. A second Muileann àrsaidh lies close by, and the two are called the elder and the younger. It follows the faith of the Church.

Muileann leathan

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 3,096

Founded 23 an Lùnastal 1942 DE by Tuathaich millers. Known for Tuathaich grain mill.

Muileann leathan of the north-west was built by Tuathaich settlers soon after the Severance to grind grain for the northern villages, which had lost the Ròdaich mills to the south. It is a small town, and its mill-race was dug by hand by the first households. It keeps the faith of the Church. Amber washed up on the nearby shore is its other trade.

Seann Skell

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,400

Founded 10 an Gearran 11,535 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for watch over the pirate waters.

Seann Skell is a Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the far north-west coast, named by the Ròdaich who resettled it; it passed to the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its citadel looks out over the waters where pirate ships are still reported and where old sailors place the Sea-Watcher. It is not the Seann Skell whose name the regiments carry, which lies far to the south-east.

  • 10 an Dùbhlachd 11,117 BDE — The tower at the north-western Seann Skell

Tobar dhearg

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 4,154

Founded 16 an Dùbhlachd 1849 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for red well of the western Tuathaich.

A Ròdaich village around a well of red water, resettled by Tuathaich families after the Severance. Like several villages of this coast it made the shrine of Manannan that it inherited its church rather than raising its own. It lives on sheep and on the market at Cathair gheal.

  • 30 am Faoilleach 2016 DE — Tobar dhearg of the hills

Siorrachd Muileann bhàn

Cnoc mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 8,008

Founded 31 an Cèitean 1606 DE by hill-lords of Muileann bhàn. Known for hill-farms above Seann Warr.

A great hill in the south, above the harbour of Seann Warr and the large mill town of Muileann bhàn. It keeps the Old Spirits, and its hill-farms supply both.

Doire dhearg

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,668

Founded 21 an t-Iuchar 1811 DE by Ròdaich miners under extraction contract. Known for red spoil-heaps of the camp years.

Doire dhearg began as a mining camp in the Age of Strangers, when the interior was first worked by the ton. Its red spoil-heaps are still visible above the village. Many of its people left when the workings moved on, and the village that remains keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Muileann bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 34,517

Founded 8 am Màrt 272 DE by a custodian house of the ore road. Known for white mills and citadel of the ore road.

Muileann bhàn is a town of thirty-four thousand with a citadel, the seat of its province, standing where the ore road from the eastern diggings met the mills. In the Age of Strangers its citadel held the human administration's weighing-house and its guards. The mills have turned to grain since the Severance, and the Old Spirits, the folk tradition of the ancestors, never lost here, have returned to the square.

Siorrachd Muileann bheag

Àth gheal

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 9,316

Founded 20 an t-Ògmhios 982 DE by farmers of Muileann bheag. Known for white ford near Seann Tarr.

Àth gheal of Muileann bheag is a ford town near Seann Tarr, founded in the long quiet centuries. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. At the great feasts it lodges the pilgrims bound for the shrine at Seann Tarr.

Baile bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,897

Founded 3 an t-Samhain 1007 DE by toll-keepers of Muileann bheag. Known for a walled town of tolls.

A small town on the road to Muileann bheag, walled to collect tolls rather than to keep enemies out. It still collects them, and has outlasted every attempt to abolish the right. It is one of several places named Baile bheag.

Cill àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,868

Founded 25 an t-Sultain 75 BDE by keepers of the Old Spirits. Known for a druids' house on an old shrine.

An ancient cell-site village in the north-east, older than the druid schools that now hold it. The founding shrine is said to have been of the Old Spirits, and its foundations lie under the present meeting-house. It is a large village supplying Muileann bheag.

Doire uaine

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,576

Founded 16 an Lùnastal 1261 BDE by the grove-keepers of the Old Spirits. Known for oak for Muileann bheag.

A green oak grove in the north-east, not the Doire uaine of the Hollow Man's hills, a confusion the library records note with some weariness. It keeps the Old Spirits and cuts its oak for Muileann bheag.

Dùn dhubh

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,841

Founded 26 an Cèitean 1817 BDE by a custodian house of Muileann bheag. Known for black fort over the coast road.

Dùn dhubh is a walled hill fort of dark stone, ranked a city though it holds under three thousand people. It commands the coast road above Muileann bheag and the harbour of Seann Toll. Its walls were raised in the Holy Age and repaired in every age after. A dubhan works stands under its walls, on the old charcoal-burners' ground.

Muileann bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,908

Founded 23 an Giblean 1210 BDE by grain-millers of the north-east. Known for flour for the north-east harbours.

A small mill that grew into a sizable town and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann bheag. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and grinds for the harbour at Ros chiar. It shares its name with three others on the island, including the Tuathaich lighthouse town.

  • 27 am Màrt 1922 DE — Muileann bheag in the north-east

Ros chiar

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,817

Founded 19 an Lùnastal 1449 DE by fishers of Muileann bheag. Known for the flour harbour of Muileann bheag.

A dusky headland harbour village on the north-east coast that ships the flour of Muileann bheag. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and competes with Seann Toll for the coast trade.

Seann Tarr

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,806

Founded 30 an Cèitean 12,927 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for north-eastern ancestor shrine.

Seann Tarr is a Seann-Dhaoine site on the north-eastern coast, resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age, and its ancestor hall is one of the oldest spirit-houses of the Old Spirits still in use. A citadel was raised over the harbour in the Age of Sundering. It is small for a city, but the shrine draws the whole north-east at the great feasts. It is the market town of the north-eastern coast, whose market began at the shrine's feasts. Honey from its heather and wax for the shrine lights are its own goods, with cheese and books, and its rope-makers are a chartered guild.

Seann Toll

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,603

Founded 19 an Giblean 10,605 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for cleft-rock harbour of the Old Ones.

Seann Toll is a harbour in a cleft of the rock, and its lowest quay is cut in a manner the Ròdaich did not use; it is held to be the work of the Seann-Dhaoine, and nothing more is known of it. The Ròdaich settled it in the Holy Age as the nearest harbour for Dùn dhubh and Muileann bheag. It is a small port town of fishers and lightermen.

Siorrachd Muileann chiar

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,790

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd 1845 DE by miners of the central diggings. Known for miners' town of the Rending.

A narrow ford-town in the central hills, grown in the Age of Strangers around the camp-roads to the diggings near Cill ghlas. The Rending, Scàineadh Cill ghlas, killed miners of this town in the collapse, and the people here still use scàinte of a man who is shaken. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Àth dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,056

Founded 20 an Giblean 1829 DE by a mining crew under the human administration. Known for straight ford of the ore carts.

Àth dhìreach was a ford where the ore carts crossed in the Age of Strangers. It is a town of three thousand in the eastern mining district. Its ford is paved with spoil from the diggings.

  • 18 an Dàmhair 525 BDE — Àth dhìreach after the poor season

Doire uaine

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,599

Founded 13 an Gearran 120 BDE by herders of the Doire uaine hills. Known for the Hollow Man of the hills.

Doire uaine is a small village in the hills where inscriptions describe the Hollow Man, something that walked without breathing and attacked anyone who lit a fire in its sight. The village was founded in the Holy Age. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Muileann chiar

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 15,578

Founded 23 an t-Iuchar 326 DE by ore-crushers of the eastern diggings. Known for ore mills of the eastern district.

Muileann chiar, seat of the province of the same name, began as an ore-crushing mill for the diggings in the hills east of the capital. It grew large in the Age of Strangers, when the district was worked by the ton, and lost its trade when Scàineadh Cill ghlas, a short way west, closed the district for a generation. It is not the silver town of the same name further east, and the two are often confused in the older records.

Muileann gheal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 688

Founded 20 an Lùnastal 1841 DE by a mining crew under the human administration. Known for walled mill-camp under Doire uaine.

Muileann gheal was a walled mill-camp under the Doire uaine hills, built in the Age of Strangers to crush ore from the eastern diggings. It is small, fewer than seven hundred people. The warm springs of Muileann ruadh lie a short walk away, and the camp's miners bathed there.

Achadh dhomhain

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 14,105

Founded 10 an t-Ògmhios 2727 BDE by farmers of Muileann chrom. Known for deep-field granaries of the camps.

Achadh dhomhain of Muileann chrom is a large farming village in deep fields, founded in the Holy Age. Its granaries fed the mining camps in the Age of Strangers and were requisitioned in the war of the Severance. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Àth ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,979

Founded 7 an t-Iuchar 285 DE by Ròdaich ferrymen of Muileann chrom. Known for the low ford and its ferry.

The low ford floods each wet season, and for part of every year the crossing is made by ferry. The town is small and has always been poor. It sends its surplus down to the quays at Inis ìseal and Ceann fhada.

Baile dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,666

Founded 28 an Lùnastal 67 DE by druid-farmers of Cnoc bhàn. Known for tithe-fields of the Cnoc bhàn druids.

A small town in a deep valley, farming for the druids of Macha at Cnoc bhàn. It has no walls and little history beyond the tithe-rolls of the druids' house, which record its harvests without a gap from the Sundering to the present.

Ceann fhada

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,509

Founded 27 an Cèitean 1320 DE by Ròdaich river pilots. Known for long quay and river pilots.

A long spit of land made Ceann fhada a landing for river craft, and its pilots have guided boats on the Abhainn uaine for centuries. It is the old rival of Inis ìseal, a short way downstream, and the two quays have quarrelled over tolls in every age the rolls cover. It prospered in the Age of Strangers carrying ore-cart loads by water and has held its trade since by carrying grain.

  • 24 an Cèitean 1928 DE — The quay at Ceann fhada seized

Cnoc fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,965

Founded 17 am Màrt 449 DE by hunters of the Muileann chrom country. Known for a walled hill by the river road.

A wild walled hill in the middle country, near the canoe-landing of Cidhe Beag on Abhainn uaine. Its walls were raised in the troubled years when the river road carried ore. It follows the order of Macha and trades with Muileann chrom and Inis ìseal.

Cuan dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,135

Founded 12 an Dàmhair 1750 DE by river fishers of the Abhainn uaine. Known for red-cliffed river landing and ferries.

Cuan dhearg is one of the ring of small river towns on the Abhainn uaine above Cathair mhòr, named for the red cliffs over its landing. It lives on the river fish and the short ferry runs between the river towns, and sends what it has for the sea down to Ceann leathan at the river mouth. It has never been walled. It is not the southern Cuan dhearg that Tonn Mhòr destroyed; the chroniclers have confused the two more than once. Its inn, An Cupa Dàna, is where Buidheann an t-Seabhaig Luaidhe, the Leaden Hawk company, gathered in the first spring of the Severance war before walking to the Hawk coast.

Doire mhòr

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,738

Founded 24 an Giblean 1858 DE by Ròdaich miners under extraction contract. Known for pit-props from a vanished oak wood.

Doire mhòr was cut out of a great oak wood in the Age of Strangers, when the workings east of the capital needed pit-props faster than any Holy Age forester would have felled them. The wood is gone and the village farms the clearing.

Inis ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,887

Founded 12 an Giblean 1071 DE by Ròdaich river boatmen. Known for river-island port on the Abhainn uaine.

Inis ìseal is a river port on a low island in the Abhainn uaine, a short way from the landing at Cidhe Beag. It is the rival of Ceann fhada a short way upstream, and the two have disputed tolls in every age. It prospered in the Age of Strangers carrying ore and has kept its trade by carrying grain.

Muileann chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 18,448

Founded 11 an Gearran 1443 BDE by Ròdaich millers on the river bend. Known for the great mill on the river bend.

The mill on the bend of the river gave its name to the town and then to the province, of which it is the seat and the largest place. It ground grain for the whole central country and, in the Age of Strangers, for the camps east of it as well. It is a busy, unwalled town that has never needed walls, standing between Cathair mhòr and Ceann leathan on the road that joins them. From the last years of the humans' rule the Company's railway ran from its pits down to the quay at Ros dhomhain, and the kingdom's Rail Board keeps its yards here. The ore line, the railway the Company laid to Cathair dhearg, was built from its yards.

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,843

Founded 26 an Gearran 758 DE by millers of Muileann chrom. Known for walled red mill.

A walled mill town on the road north of Muileann chrom, one of three places named Muileann dhearg. It was walled in the Age of Strangers to protect its stores. It follows the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Seann Toll

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,455

Founded 8 an Gearran 12,832 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the rock-hollow landing and Còmhrag crowds.

A Seann-Dhaoine river port on the Abhainn uaine in the midlands, called Seann Toll by the Ròdaich for the hollow in the rock where its boats lie. It is walled and follows the order of Macha, and it stands a short way west of Cill ghlas, where the Rending opened. It lies close to Ceann leathan at the river mouth, where the Còmhrag is fought each year, and fighters from the tournament fill its taverns.

Siorrachd Muileann dhearg

Baile thais

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 13,140

Founded 5 an t-Ògmhios 913 BDE by river-boatmen of the Abhainn uaine. Known for Cidhe Beag landing on the Abhainn uaine.

Baile thais stands on the Abhainn uaine where the river leaves the hills for its run down to the gulf, and the river landing of Cidhe Beag lies just downstream. Boats have been launched here since the Holy Age to carry goods inland and ore down. It is a busy, unwalled town of boatmen and warehouses. Slighe-mhara Caol fhiadhaich, the southern sea-lane, ends at the landing of Cidhe Beag below the town.

Cill fhada

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,783

Founded 17 an Dùbhlachd 57 DE by druids of Macha. Known for the long temple of Macha.

A temple-site village strung along a long ridge near Baile chrom, whose temple of Macha is the longest building in the district. It farms for the market at Baile chrom and sends its grain to the tithe-granaries there.

Cill ghlas

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,711

Founded 4 am Faoilleach 1185 BDE by a house of the druid schools. Known for Scàineadh Cill ghlas, the Rending.

Cill ghlas, the grey cell, was a quiet village of the druid schools in the hills east of the capital until the Age of Strangers pushed the workings under it. Late in that age a routine excavation tore open a fault around it, killing dozens and closing the working; the Rending gave the island the word 'scàinte'. The village was rebuilt on the far side of the crack, and its people still mark the day of the dead.

Cnoc chaol

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 655

Founded 22 an Cèitean 1850 DE by a mining crew under the human administration. Known for a spent camp on the narrow hill.

Cnoc chaol was a mining camp on the narrow hill, worked by the ton in the Age of Strangers. It emptied after Scàineadh Cill ghlas closed the district and never recovered. Fewer than seven hundred people live there now, among the spoil heaps.

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 22,453

Founded 2 an t-Ògmhios 1820 BDE by Ròdaich millers of the central country. Known for stamping mills turned to grain.

The red mill is the seat of its province and one of the largest towns of the centre, standing between Seann Chwen and Cnoc ghorm. Its mills stamped ore in the Age of Strangers and turned back to grain after the Severance. It is a town of the capital's order, the order of Macha, busy and unwalled.

  • 25 an Giblean 1218 BDE — The bronze-casters of Muileann dhearg

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 14,052

Founded 30 an t-Sultain 38 BDE by ore-millers of the central diggings. Known for red mill beside Cill ghlas.

Muileann dhearg, seat of its province, is a mill town a short way from Cill ghlas. Scàineadh Cill ghlas tore open the hills nearby and killed dozens, and the town's mills stood idle for a generation after. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Siorrachd Muileann dhomhain

Achadh chaol

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,691

Founded 23 am Faoilleach 527 DE by Ròdaich farmers of Muileann dhomhain. Known for narrow fields feeding the diggings.

A village of narrow fields that has fed the eastern mining district since the district was opened. Scàineadh Cill ghlas, the Rending, struck it when the fault tore open, and the diggings it fed were closed after. It still sends its grain to the mills around it. The village stands on land the custodians of Muileann dhomhain lent to the people of the closed district at Coinneachadh an Fhearainn, the standing stone on the moor road.

  • 5 an Dùbhlachd 1916 DE — Achadh chaol raised by the displaced

Achadh ìseal

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,104

Founded 27 an t-Sultain 1145 DE by farmers from Muileann dhomhain. Known for harvests for the southern mills.

A low field village in the south-east, farming for the mill town of Muileann dhomhain and the port of Ceann chaol. It keeps the Old Spirits and has no history the chroniclers found worth writing beyond its harvests.

Caol naomh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,711

Founded 17 an Giblean 442 DE by druids of Òrd Bhrìde. Known for pilgrim landing of Òrd Bhrìde.

A holy strait-harbour near the ruins of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, where the orthodox order of Brìde's flame built a landing for pilgrims coming to the mountain of Crom's stone. It is one of the few towns where Òrd Bhrìde holds the majority, and its druids were among those who formalized the order's rite in the first years of the new kingdom. It is a small town and quiet outside the pilgrim season. Pilgrims' boats from the southern Seann Skell come round to its landing by Slighe-mhara chritheanach, the shaking sea-way, named for the swell off the south cape.

Ceann chaol

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 9,536

Founded 23 an Giblean 946 DE by Ròdaich seafarers of the narrow point. Known for narrow-point harbour, rival of Ceann mhin.

Ceann chaol is a port city on the narrow point, and the old rival of Ceann mhin along the same shore. Its ships carry the flour of Muileann dhomhain and the grain of the eastern plain. The two harbours have disputed fishing grounds in every age, and the disputes are recorded at length.

  • 4 am Màrt 2848 BDE — The carriers' path to Ceann chaol
  • 20 an t-Samhain 1882 DE — The deep quay at Ceann chaol

Muileann dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 16,277

Founded 8 an t-Iuchar 1252 BDE by the millers of the deep race. Known for the grain-exchange of the south-east.

A mill on a deep, fast race in the central country and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann dhomhain. It was a milling town for centuries and grew rich carrying grain to the mining settlements in the Age of Strangers, when the camps could no longer feed themselves. It keeps the Old Spirits of the Ròdaich, and its grain-exchange still sets the price of flour for the south-east.

  • 5 an Dùbhlachd 1896 DE — The strikebreakers of Muileann dhomhain

Muileann dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 20,506

Founded 9 an t-Samhain 1582 BDE by Ròdaich millers of the south-east. Known for deep mill-pools feeding Ceann chaol's ships.

Muileann dhomhain, seat of its province, is a town of twenty thousand built around deep mill-pools fed from the hills. Its flour goes down to the quays of Ceann chaol and out by sea, and the two towns have depended on each other since the Holy Age. It is not the smaller Muileann dhomhain of Dùn ìseal to the north.
