  • 5 an Lùnastal 1065 DE — Muileann dhomhain resettled

Muileann uaine

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,705

Founded 8 am Màrt 1827 DE by a human milling concern with Ròdaich labour. Known for ore-crushing mill of the interior workings.

Muileann uaine was built in the Age of Strangers as a crushing mill for ore from the interior workings. It is not the Muileann uaine of the Cnoc bheag country that the Green Death struck, though the two are often confused. It is a small town now and keeps the orthodox rite of Òrd Bhrìde.

Siorrachd Muileann leathan

Baile fhionn

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,628

Founded 31 an Dàmhair 1733 DE by Ròdaich farmers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for trade across the line with Baile ruadh.

A small fair town in the north-west, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It follows the Tuathaich Church and trades across the line with the Ròdaich town of Baile ruadh.

Baile leathan

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,609

Founded 21 an t-Iuchar 1802 DE by human settlers from an Tìr Thall. Known for an old strangers' settlement of the north.

Baile leathan was built by human settlers in the Age of Strangers on the northern coast, one of the few places the strangers founded rather than took. After the Severance it became a Tuathaich town. It keeps the faith of the Church and its oldest families still count their descent from the Crossing.

Cill chaol

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,898

Founded 10 am Màrt 985 BDE by Ròdaich druids; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for a Tuathaich church in a Ròdaich chapel.

Cill chaol was a narrow Ròdaich chapel village near the northern coast, emptied at the Severance and taken by Tuathaich families. They made its chapel a church of the Tuathaich, and the Ròdaich carvings on its doorposts were left in place beside theirs. It is a small place near the lighthouse of Muileann bheag.

Cnoc leathan

fort · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,319

Founded 9 an t-Samhain 1793 DE by the human administration, as a coast fort. Known for Tuathaich-held fort on the north coast.

Cnoc leathan was built by the human administration as a fort on the northern coast road, not far from the lighthouse at Muileann bheag. The Tuathaich have held it since the Severance and keep its citadel manned. Its small garrison follows the Tuathaich Church.

Muileann bheag

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,177

Founded 14 an Giblean 1491 DE by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for Taigh-solais Muileann bheag.

A small mill town on the north coast beside Taigh-solais Muileann bheag, one of the five lighthouses built in the Age of Strangers. It became Tuathaich at the Severance, and the Tuathaich lighthouse-keepers tended the beacon for the kingdom until it was converted to dubhan. It follows the Tuathaich Church.

  • 13 am Faoilleach 1843 DE — The fishermen of Muileann bheag

Muileann leathan

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 22,366

Founded 24 an Giblean 2880 BDE by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the Tuathaich mill-citadel.

A wide mill on a northern stream, walled with a citadel, and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann leathan. It was a Ròdaich town until the Severance, when the Tuathaich took it over as one of the principal towns of their homeland. It is a centre of the Tuathaich Church, and its keep is where the Tuathaich northern coast is governed.

Siorrachd Muileann mhin

Doire bheag

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 693

Founded 4 an t-Samhain 1521 DE by Ròdaich woodcutters of the capital. Known for firewood for the capital.

A small village in an oak copse north-east of Cathair dhearg, which has cut firewood and charcoal for the capital for as long as there are accounts. It has never grown past seven hundred people. Its people follow the capital's order, the order of Macha and take their wood into the city on market days.

Muileann mhin

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 30,105

Founded 20 an t-Iuchar 1541 BDE by millers of the capital country. Known for the capital's flour mills.

Muileann mhin is a large river town on the Abhainn fhionn east of the capital and the seat of its province. Its flour mills have fed the capital since the Holy Age. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha and ships its flour down the river to Cathair dhomhain and along the shore to Cathair dhearg and Ros dhomhain.

Siorrachd Muileann naomh

Àth chrom

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,343

Founded 3 an t-Iuchar 950 DE by Ròdaich drovers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for Tuathaich drovers at the bent ford.

A drovers' town at the bent ford, Ròdaich until the Severance and Tuathaich since. It lies a short way from the field of Àth leathan, and its people carried the dead from that battle. It follows the faith of the Church.

  • 30 an t-Samhain 1929 DE — The columns at Àth chrom

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,961

Founded 3 an Gearran 1036 DE by Ròdaich traders of Muileann naomh. Known for straight-street twin of Cnoc gheal.

A small town of one straight street on the far west, twinned with Cnoc gheal a short walk away. It lies close to the Tuathaich line and trades with the villages beyond it. It follows the order of Manannan.

Caol ruadh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,899

Founded 22 an t-Iuchar 992 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the red strait. Known for red strait and the orthodox rite of Brìde's flame.

Caol ruadh takes its name from the red rock of the strait it watches on the southern coast. It was a quiet fishing town for most of its history, and was among the first to take up the orthodox rite of Brìde's flame and Crom's stone when Òrd Bhrìde was formalized. Since An Cogadh Fada its harbour has victualled the garrisons and fleet stationed at Seann Skell close by. It was chartered as the sixteenth market town after An Cogadh Fada, to victual the garrisons and the fleet.

  • 14 an Giblean 5031 BDE — Caol ruadh on the southern strait
  • 26 am Faoilleach 2022 DE — The market charter of Caol ruadh

Cill gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,948

Founded 27 an Lùnastal 1073 BDE by Ròdaich druids of the western coast. Known for rough stone shrine of the west.

A village around a rough stone shrine on the far western coast of the Ròdaich country. Its shrine is older than any of its houses, and Manannan was worshipped there before the orders divided. It is a small village of fewer than two thousand.

Cnoc dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,714

Founded 31 an Lùnastal 605 DE by potters of the west. Known for red-clay potteries of the west.

Cnoc dhearg of Muileann naomh is a small town of the west, founded in the long quiet centuries on a hill of red clay. Its potteries supply jars and tiles to the western harbours, and the Age of Strangers brought it a brief trade in crucibles for the assayers. It keeps the order of Manannan.

Cnoc gheal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,713

Founded 16 am Màrt 745 DE by Ròdaich druids of the order of Manannan. Known for white hill shrine of Manannan.

The Ròdaich Cnoc gheal is a white hill with a shrine of Manannan mac Lir, twinned with Baile dhìreach. A second Cnoc gheal, held by the Tuathaich, lies a short walk north-east over the line. The two villages share a name and very little else, not even a faith.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 752

Founded 31 am Faoilleach 1931 DE by the restored kingdom, as a border post. Known for border walls facing the Tuathaich.

Cnoc òg, "the young hill", was walled by the restored kingdom soon after the Severance, on the Ròdaich side of the line facing the Tuathaich towns to the north and west. It has never been more than a small town of soldiers' families and carters. In An Cogadh Fada it lay a short march behind the field at Àth leathan, and its walls held the wounded after that first battle.

Muileann naomh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,137

Founded 4 an t-Ògmhios 2400 BDE by druids of the order of Manannan. Known for the consecrated mill-wheel.

A holy mill in the west, the seat of Siorrachd Muileann naomh, whose wheel is said to have been consecrated to Manannan mac Lir. It lies near the Àth leathan battlefield and was taken over by crown regiments in the Long War. It follows the order of Manannan.

  • 6 an Dùbhlachd 1868 DE — Muileann naomh buys its way out

Muileann naomh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,401

Founded 16 an t-Iuchar 88 DE by druids of Òrd Bhrìde. Known for grain blessed by the druids of Brìde's flame.

A holy mill in the south, the seat of Siorrachd Muileann naomh, whose druids of the orthodox order of Brìde's flame bless the grain before it is ground. It is one of the few towns of Òrd Bhrìde and trades with Caol ruadh and Seann Skell. Its hawk-house was the southernmost of Òrd an t-Seabhaig, the first on Rodos to hang a bronze bell, until it took Òrd Bhrìde's written order in the first years of the restored kingdom; the bell now rings for Brìde's flame.

Siorrachd Muileann shean

Àth fhionn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,707

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd 658 DE by fishers of the north coast. Known for fair ford of the north coast.

Àth fhionn of Muileann shean is a ford town of the north coast, founded in the long quiet centuries where the coast road crosses a clear stream. It shares the watch-fire of Cnoc gheal and trades with the harbour of Cill leathan. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith. It is the market town of the north coast. Fish, whale-oil and wool come to its strand-market, and its whale-boats go out every summer.

  • 19 an Gearran 796 DE — The strand-market at Àth fhionn
  • 9 an Dùbhlachd 1834 DE — Whale-boats out of Àth fhionn

Cill leathan

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 9,956

Founded 27 am Màrt 1310 BDE by keepers of the north-coast cell. Known for broad cell and its sea citadel.

Cill leathan is a large harbour village of the north coast, founded as a cell in the Holy Age. A citadel was raised over its harbour in the Age of Strangers to guard the human ships that used it. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Cnoc bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,848

Founded 8 an Lùnastal 740 DE by farmers of the north coast. Known for north-coast hill farms.

Cnoc bheag of Muileann shean is a small town of hill farms on the north coast, founded in the long quiet centuries. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith. Its people send their sons to the druid teachers at Cill àrsaidh.

Cnoc gheal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,566

Founded 20 an t-Iuchar 1138 DE by watchmen of the north. Known for white-hill watchtower of the north coast.

Cnoc gheal is a white hill with a small citadel, raised as a watchtower in the long quiet centuries to give warning of ships on the northern coast. Its fire could be seen from Cill leathan and Àth fhionn, and the three kept a common watch. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith, and its garrison is now a handful of old soldiers and their families.

Muileann shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 19,610

Founded 1 an t-Samhain 1906 BDE by the first millers of the northern river. Known for the oldest mill-wheel in the north.

The old mill of the north, whose wheel the Holy Age king-lists already call ancient, and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann shean. Its walls went up in the Age of Strangers, when it ground grain for the mining camps on contract and was raided for it. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and owns the well-village of Tobar ìseal below it.

  • 10 an Gearran 1833 BDE — Muileann shean on the northern road

  • 19 an Giblean 1988 DE — Muileann shean's school of hewers

Siorrachd Ros bheag

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,760

Founded 18 an Lùnastal 393 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the west. Known for western fishing and war-supply landing.

A low harbour on the western coast, sheltered by Ros bheag, which it has always served as a lesser port. Its people follow the order of Manannan, the order that runs along the west. The fighting of the Long War at Àth leathan was near enough that the harbour carried supplies for the crown's regiments.

Dùn thais

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,302

Founded 23 an Gearran 857 BDE by custodians of the western hills. Known for hill citadel of the western coast.

Dùn thais, the damp fort, is a hill stronghold above the western coast, held by custodians of the vein's western road since the Holy Age. Its walls were rebuilt in the Age of Strangers, when the western harbours began shipping ore, and its citadel has never stood empty since. In An Cogadh Fada its garrison marched to the field of Àth leathan, a short road to the north-east.

  • 3 an Dàmhair 1966 DE — Dùn thais in the west

Ros àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,072

Founded 16 an t-Ògmhios 1778 BDE by custodians of the western headland. Known for walled harbour on the ancient headland.

Ros àrsaidh is a small walled harbour on an ancient headland of the west, fortified by the Holy Age custodians. It lies within the province of Ros bheag and has always stood in the shadow of that citadel. It keeps the order of Manannan. The coast road north from Ros bheag, Ceum Ros àrsaidh, starts below its walls; Strake's constables held it in the last months of the Severance war.

  • 3 an Dàmhair 1929 DE — Outposts at Ros àrsaidh

Ros bheag

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 23,817

Founded 4 am Faoilleach 1362 BDE by custodians of the western coast. Known for citadel harbour of the western coast.

Ros bheag is the citadel harbour and provincial seat of the western coast, holding Dùn thais and Ros àrsaidh within its province. It was fortified in the Holy Age and has been the western sea's naval station through every age since. Its people keep the order of Manannan. It is the market town of the west coast, and its own trade is in books, boots and salted food.

Siorrachd Ros dhomhain

Doire fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,507

Founded 18 an Dùbhlachd 1467 DE by woodcutters of the wild oak wood. Known for oaks said to have built the Sundering fleet.

Doire fhiadhaich was a wild oak wood on the capital shore, and tradition holds that timber for the Sundering fleet was felled here. The wood is long gone and the village is now a fishing quarter between Ros dhomhain and the capital's harbours. It has kept its village rank and its own fishing rights.

Ros dhomhain

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 51,589

Founded 27 am Faoilleach 1232 DE by merchant families of the capital shore. Known for the capital country's great merchant port.

Ros dhomhain is the most populous place of the capital country, a merchant port that outgrew every wall it was ever given until no one built another. The first human traders lodged here after the Crossing, and its counting-houses have served every master of the island's trade since. It sits between the capital and the old harbour of Seann Vell, and the three have run together into one shore. The Company's railway, the ore line, came down to its deep-water quay from the pits at Muileann chrom in the last years of Edward Vane's commission, and the first steamer seen on Rodos had come into its harbour half a century before. In the present year its quay became the one place on the island where dubhan may be loaded for beyond the island, under the charter Dubhan won from the council: a clerk of the Treasury takes the tithe on every barrel, and the custodians of Brìde's order seal every hold.

Seann Vell

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,072

Founded 29 an Lùnastal 4041 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for old quay stones of the capital shore.

Seann Vell on the capital shore stands on Seann-Dhaoine quay stones, still visible at low water beneath the later harbour. The Ròdaich resettled it in the Holy Age and walled it in the long quiet centuries. It has since been drawn into the sprawl of Ros dhomhain, but keeps its own walls and its own harbour-master. Its scent-makers distil the best-known scent on the island.

Siorrachd Ros gharbh

Cnoc gharbh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,691

Founded 5 an Giblean 975 DE by quarriers of Ros gharbh. Known for quarries on the rough hill.

Cnoc gharbh is a rough hill of quarries near Seann Bhral, whose walls were built of its stone. It is a town of nearly five thousand, of quarrymen and carters. The standing column at Cnoc ghorm is not of its stone, a fact its masons have checked more than once.

  • 25 an Giblean 1856 DE — The huts of Cnoc gharbh

Ros gharbh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 19,021

Founded 3 am Faoilleach 216 DE by fishers of the rough headland. Known for the gulf's fishing fleet.

Ros gharbh is a harbour town on a rough headland of the gulf and the seat of its province. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and grew with the gulf's fishing fleet. Tonn Mhòr Cnoc chaol, the Great Wave, ran up the gulf in 1933, broke its quays and threw the fleet onto the headland, though the town on its height lost few people. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

  • 31 an Dàmhair 1858 DE — Fish smuggled from Ros gharbh

Seann Bhral

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,945

Founded 9 an t-Samhain 5524 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for walled old harbour of Ros gharbh.

Seann Bhral is a walled harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site, settled by the Ròdaich and named by them for the Old Ones. It lies near Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, the ruined outpost no one can date. It is a port town of four thousand.

Siorrachd Ros gheal

Ros gheal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 26,562

Founded 29 an Dùbhlachd 1990 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the white headland. Known for white headland and the disputed bay.

Ros gheal, Ros leathan and Seann Skell share one bay on the north-central coast, and have quarrelled over its moorings for as long as the rolls run. Ros gheal is the largest of the three and the seat of its province. Its people keep the Hawk order's rite of Mòd, and its white headland is the first land the northern fishing boats see coming home.

Ros leathan

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,619

Founded 30 am Faoilleach 1735 DE by Ròdaich fishers of the Hawk bay. Known for rival wharves of the Hawk bay.

Ros leathan is a harbour town on the Hawk bay, sharing it with Ros gheal and Seann Skell. It was founded in the long quiet centuries by fishers who would not pay Ros gheal's mooring dues. It keeps the Hawk order of the Old Faith.

Siorrachd Seann Bhral

Muileann chiar

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 8,751

Founded 10 an t-Iuchar 200 DE by millers of the Seann Bhral country. Known for the other Muileann chiar.

A dusky mill town with a citadel in the south-east, not the silver town of the same name further north; the confusion of the two is an old grievance here. It grinds for Àth chiar and the harbour of Seann Bhral. It keeps the Old Spirits.

Seann Bhral

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 49,681

Founded 30 an Lùnastal 12,578 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the south-east's great walled harbour.

Seann Bhral of the south-east is a Seann-Dhaoine site that the Ròdaich resettled in the Holy Age, and it has grown into the greatest harbour of that coast and the seat of its province. It was walled in the Age of Strangers, when its quays shipped ore from the interior. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Siorrachd Seann Bhrenn

Àth fhionn

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,819

Founded 8 am Màrt 2761 BDE by the ford-keepers of Seann Bhrenn. Known for the fair ford.

A fair ford in the north below the city of Dùn thais, on the road from the Seann-Dhaoine harbour at Seann Bhrenn. It keeps the Old Spirits of the Ròdaich and remains a small crossing town.

Seann Bhrenn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 17,305

Founded 12 an Giblean 12,930 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the northern Seann-Dhaoine harbour.

A Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the north coast, called Seann Bhrenn by the Ròdaich, and the seat of the shire of the same name. It is a large village of the Old Spirits, and its fishers tell that the harbour-stones were laid by people who had no need of the Ròdaich's tides.

Siorrachd Seann Chwen

Àth chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,741

Founded 19 an t-Samhain 662 DE by ford-keepers of the Seann Chwen country. Known for bent ford south of Cill ghlas.

A small ford on a bent stream south of Cill ghlas, where the Rending opened. It follows the order of Macha.

Baile ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,672

Founded 5 an t-Ògmhios 1273 DE by farmers of the Seann Chwen country. Known for grain town south of Cill ghlas.

A low town in the middle east, a short way south of Cill ghlas and the ground the Rending tore open. It follows the order of Macha and sends its grain to the harbour at Seann Chwen.

Baile òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,732

Founded 6 an Dàmhair 1819 DE by a mining crew under the human administration. Known for camp-town of the Cill ghlas diggings.

Baile òg, "the young town", was a camp of the diggings east of the capital, raised in the Age of Strangers near Cill ghlas. It emptied when Scàineadh Cill ghlas closed the district for a generation. It was reopened after the Severance, and its people now follow the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Cathair naomh

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 14,058

Founded 1 an Gearran 158 BDE by druids of the capital's order. Known for the druids' city by the old outpost.

A holy city near the ruins of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, built by the druids of Macha in the Holy Age as a seat of learning. The ruins are said to have been older than any Ròdaich memory when the city was founded, and the druids left them as they were. It is unwalled and trades with the harbour of Seann Chwen and with Ceann leathan.

Ceann leathan

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,870

Founded 19 an t-Samhain 2816 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the gulf. Known for Còmhrag Ceann leathan, the annual melee.

Ceann leathan, the broad headland, is a walled temple city on the gulf, older than most of the harbours around it. Its temple of Macha is the chief house of her order in the gulf towns. Since the early years of the restored kingdom it has held Còmhrag Ceann leathan, the brutal annual melee, which draws fighters and crowds from every province. It is the market town of the gulf and the old vein country, fifty-two towns in all, and the dearest market on Rodos. Its own trade is in cheese and salted food, and its yards build seagoing hulls.

Muileann fhionn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,965

Founded 1 an Cèitean 1365 DE by millers of the Ceann leathan country. Known for grain milled for two landings.

A fair-stoned walled mill town between Ceann leathan and Cuan dhearg, grinding grain landed at Ceann leathan's harbour and Cuan dhearg's river landing. Its walls went up in the Age of Strangers. It follows the order of Macha.

Ros bhàn

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,591

Founded 24 an Lùnastal 65 DE by the garrison of the gulf mouth. Known for fortified headland at the gulf mouth.

Ros bhàn is a fortified headland at the mouth of the gulf, walled and given a citadel in the long quiet centuries to guard the harbours within. It is a city by rank, though most of its people are soldiers, customs clerks and their families. The white stone of its headland gives it its name. The customs town also boils soap and blows glass for the gulf.

Ros ruadh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,551

Founded 27 am Faoilleach 61 DE by quarrymen of the red headland. Known for red stone for the gulf cities.

Ros ruadh is a small harbour on the gulf, founded by quarrymen who shipped its red stone to the gulf cities. Much of Ceann leathan and Ros bhàn is built of it. It keeps a ferry to the harbours across the water.

Seann Chwen

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 36,527

Founded 19 an Giblean 12,736 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the gulf's chief harbour and fish-market.

The larger Seann Chwen is the chief harbour of the gulf and the seat of the province that bears its name, built on a Seann-Dhaoine site the Ròdaich resettled in the Holy Age. It takes the fish of the gulf and the goods of Cathair mhòr. It has no walls; the fortified headlands of Ros bhàn and Ceann leathan stand to either side of it.

Siorrachd Seann Dunn

Àth ghorm

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,701

Founded 28 an Giblean 1364 DE by ford-keepers of Seann Dunn. Known for the toll-ford of Seann Dunn.

A blue ford with a small citadel on the road inland from Seann Dunn, built to hold the crossing for the harbour. It follows the order of Macha and is a small town of carters and toll-keepers.

Baile fhada

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,593

Founded 27 an Dùbhlachd 681 DE by Ròdaich soldiers of the capital's south. Known for long street and citadel south of the capital.

A town of one long street with a citadel at its end, south-east of the capital. It was a garrison town in the Age of Strangers and has kept its citadel manned since. Its people are soldiers' families and carters, and its street is the last stage of the road from the southern coast to Cathair dhearg.

Seann Chwen

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,351

Founded 1 am Faoilleach 12,033 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for citadel on the capital's southern sea road.

The landing stones at Seann Chwen are of the Seann-Dhaoine, and the name was given by the Ròdaich who resettled the site in the Holy Age. It is a small harbour on the south shore, but its citadel guards the capital's southern sea road, and it has been garrisoned more often than its size would suggest. Its people keep the order of Macha, the capital's order of the Old Faith, and its green is one of the two grounds where the travelling circus, An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn, pitches.

  • 11 an Cèitean 1929 DE — The other Seann Chwen

Seann Dunn

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 14,296

Founded 28 am Faoilleach 12,773 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the Seann-Dhaoine harbour-mole.

The Seann-Dhaoine left the harbour-mole and the name Dunn; the Ròdaich called it Seann Dunn and built a citadel over the mole. It is the seat of the shire of the same name and follows the order of Macha. It is a village in form but large in number, with the ford-town of Àth ghorm under its protection.

  • 6 an Gearran 11,277 BDE — The whale-rib houses of Seann Dunn

Siorrachd Seann Skell

Achadh gheal

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 9,194

Founded 23 an t-Samhain 959 BDE by Ròdaich flax-growers of Seann Skell. Known for flax fields and bleached linen.

The white field is the flax country that feeds the linen-weavers of Seann Skell, and in the drying season the whole plain is laid with bleaching cloth. The village is large and prosperous for its kind, and it follows the order of Manannan as the river port does. Its growers' guild has sold to the same Seann Skell houses for longer than either side can prove.

Achadh ghlas

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,980

Founded 26 an Lùnastal 1658 BDE by Ròdaich farmers of Seann Skell. Known for grey fields on the Seann Skell road.

A village of grey-green fields on the road north from Seann Skell, whose barley and oats feed the great river port. It lies just south of the Tuathaich line, and since the Severance its farmers have ploughed with one eye on the boundary. In the Long War its barns quartered soldiers of the seventh regiment on the way to Àth leathan.

Àth chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,227

Founded 21 am Màrt 1232 DE by fishers of the west. Known for bent ford on the lower Abhainn naomh.

Àth chrom, the bent ford, is a river town at a bend of the Abhainn naomh in the west, below Seann Skell, whose boats go down to the sea at Ros àrsaidh. It was founded in the long quiet centuries. Since An Cogadh Fada, troops of the regiment named for Seann Skell have been quartered close by.

Àth fhionn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,754

Founded 13 an t-Samhain 1743 DE by farmers of the south-east. Known for ford town beside the Seann Skell garrisons.

Àth fhionn of Seann Skell is a ford town of the south-east. It was founded in the long quiet centuries. Since An Cogadh Fada it has billeted soldiers of the regiments stationed at Seann Skell nearby. It keeps the orthodox rite of Òrd Bhrìde.

Àth leathan

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 680

Founded 8 am Màrt 1264 DE by Ròdaich drovers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for the first battlefield of the Long War.

A Ròdaich drovers' village at the wide ford, emptied at the Severance and resettled by Tuathaich families sent north. In the years before the Long War it became a gathering place for the coal-holdouts of the north-west. The Battle of Àth leathan, the first major engagement of An Cogadh Fada, was fought on the meadows just west of the ford, and the town has not recovered its numbers since.

Àth shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,697

Founded 9 an t-Ògmhios 1073 BDE by Ròdaich keepers of the northern ford. Known for old ford on the northern march.

An old ford on the road north out of the Ròdaich country, walled in the Age of Strangers and strengthened again after the Severance, when the Tuathaich country began a short way to the west. It is a town of the Hawk order, Òrd an t-Seabhaig, and its temple is one of the oldest of the order, whose rite is the older form of Òrd Bhrìde's. It trades with Inis bhàn to the south and, warily, with the Tuathaich villages over the line.

Àth uaine

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 10,807

Founded 3 an Giblean 2858 BDE by ford-keepers of Seann Skell. Known for green ford inland of Seann Skell.

Àth uaine of Seann Skell is a ford town inland of the Hawk bay, founded in the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. It is the market for the three quarrelling harbours of the bay.

Doire ghorm

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,552

Founded 26 an t-Sultain 1755 DE by charcoal-burners of the south-east. Known for charcoal for the south-coast smithies.

Doire ghorm is a grove village of the south-east, founded by charcoal-burners in the long quiet centuries. Its charcoal once fed the smithies of the south coast. It keeps the orthodox rite of Brìde's flame, like its neighbours.

Doire naomh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,068

Founded 14 an t-Iuchar 1214 BDE by druids of the order of Manannan. Known for graves of the Àth leathan dead.

A holy oak grove in the west near Àth leathan, where the Long War's first battle was fought. It stayed Ròdaich and kept the order of Manannan, and it buried many of the dead of that battle in its grove. The grove is closed to strangers.

Inis àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,121

Founded 28 am Faoilleach 2923 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the west. Known for river port near the field of Àth leathan.

Inis àrsaidh is an island town on the Abhainn naomh in the west, founded in the Holy Age; its ships put to sea from Ros àrsaidh at the river mouth. It was the nearest river port to the field of Àth leathan, and in An Cogadh Fada it supplied the state's forces for the first battle. Its fairground is one of the two grounds where the travelling circus, An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn, pitches.

  • 12 an t-Sultain 34 BDE — The trial hull lost off Inis àrsaidh's harbour
  • 2 an Gearran 305 DE — The deep hull that would not float true

Muileann chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,454

Founded 22 an Cèitean 1187 DE by Ròdaich millers of the Seann Skell country. Known for a Ròdaich mill on the Tuathaich line.

A crooked mill on the edge of the north-west, left in Ròdaich hands when the Tuathaich homeland was fixed around it. It keeps the order of Manannan, whose sea-feasts its Tuathaich neighbours keep beside their church's, and its millers have ground for both peoples since the Severance, which the chroniclers note without comment. Cnoc ghlas and Àth àrsaidh over the line buy its flour.

Seann Skell

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 22,120

Founded 19 an t-Samhain 11,340 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for walled old harbour of the Hawk bay.

Seann Skell of the Hawk bay is a walled harbour city on a Seann-Dhaoine site, sharing its bay with Ros gheal and Ros leathan. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age and walled in the Age of Sundering. It keeps the Hawk order of the Old Faith. It is the market town of the Hawk bay and the north-central coast. Amber from the bay's strands is the one good it sells to other markets, and its yards build seagoing hulls.

Seann Skell

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 57,907

Founded 29 am Faoilleach 4937 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the southern fleet harbour.

Seann Skell is the great southern port, a town of nearly sixty thousand whose harbour lies on a site the Seann-Dhaoine used before the Ròdaich; the name keeps their root. It is the seat of its province and a centre of Òrd Bhrìde, the order of Brìde's flame. The ninth regiment and the second fleet, raised in the Long War, are stationed here. It shares its name with the great western river port. Glass is blown there from the white sand of its own shore.

Seann Skell

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 74,120

Founded 6 an Gearran 12,522 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the great western river port.

Seann Skell is the great river port of the west, a city of seventy-four thousand and the largest place on the island, whose barges run down the Abhainn naomh to Ros àrsaidh; its river harbour is a Seann-Dhaoine site and the name keeps their root. It is walled by its citadel rather than by curtain walls, and the seventh regiment, raised in the Long War, is stationed here. The first battle of that war was fought at Àth leathan, a short march north.

Siorrachd Seann Tarr

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,748

Founded 6 an Gearran 770 DE by harbour-folk of Seann Tarr. Known for fishing the eastern narrows.

A narrow harbour ford in the far east, close to the old Seann-Dhaoine harbour of Seann Tarr. It keeps the Old Spirits and sends its fishing to the market at Cnoc uaine.

Baile mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 4,675

Founded 15 an t-Samhain 1214 DE by craftsmen outside the walls of Baile Mòr ruadh. Known for trades outside Baile Mòr ruadh's walls.

Baile mhòr grew outside the walls of Baile Mòr ruadh, a suburb of tanners, dyers and other trades the city would not have within its gates. It has never been walled itself. In the Age of Strangers it was burned once in a quarrel between the city and the administration, and rebuilt in stone.

Baile Mòr ruadh

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 15,158

Founded 25 an t-Sultain 2717 BDE by a custodian house of the eastern shore. Known for red-stone walls of the east.

Baile Mòr ruadh is a walled city of red stone, crowned by a citadel, and the strongest place of its province, though the seat of the shire is the old harbour of Seann Tarr. It was fought over in the Age of Strangers, when the human administration made it a district seat, and when the shires were drawn the seat went back to Seann Tarr. Its walls show repairs of every age. Travellers on the eastern road break their journey at An Taigh-seinnse Òir just west of the city. Its dyers make the reds and blues of the east, and it is one of the chief towns of the east for books and ink.

  • 15 an Lùnastal 4290 BDE — Baile Mòr ruadh in the east
  • 18 an Dàmhair 1480 DE — Baile Mòr ruadh's fair
  • 25 an Giblean 1888 DE — Drought-fever at Baile Mòr ruadh

Baile ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 7,717

Founded 25 an t-Samhain 33 DE by herders of Seann Tarr. Known for supplier to Taigh-solais Baile ìseal.

Baile ruadh is a farm town near the eastern coast, founded in the long quiet centuries. Since the lighthouses were built its people have supplied the keepers of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal on the coast beyond. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Ceann chiar

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,169

Founded 10 an Dùbhlachd 807 DE by Ròdaich fishers of the eastern coast. Known for walled harbour against pirates.

Ceann chiar is a walled harbour on the eastern coast, walled against the pirate ships that have been seen in these waters in every age. It keeps a watch-fire on its headland. It is the port of Seann Tarr province.

  • 8 an Giblean 5184 BDE — The sharing holds after the Black Wind
  • 12 an Cèitean 3875 BDE — The Black Wind remembered at Ceann chiar

Doire fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,947

Founded 11 am Màrt 1078 DE by Ròdaich woodwards of Seann Tarr. Known for wild oakwood and boar.

A village in a wild oakwood between Baile Mòr ruadh and the east coast. It lives on timber and on the boar hunts that the city's families come out for. It keeps the Old Spirits.

Seann Tarr

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 23,042

Founded 25 an Giblean 12,039 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the old eastern harbour and fleet.

A harbour of the Seann-Dhaoine on the eastern coast, named Seann Tarr by the Ròdaich, and the seat of the shire of the same name. It is a large village that follows the Old Spirits. The eastern pirates made it unsafe in the Age of Strangers, and it has a small fleet of its own.

  • 5 an Giblean 11,595 BDE — The script appears at Seann Tarr
  • 3 an Gearran 1360 DE — The grey storm at Seann Tarr

Siorrachd Seann Toll

Cathair naomh

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 12,935

Founded 22 an Dùbhlachd 4439 BDE by unknown builders, later the Ròdaich keepers of the Old Spirits. Known for the unwalled ring of the ancestors.

The holy city of the north grew around a ring of stones older than the Ròdaich, and the chroniclers do not claim to know who raised them. The Ròdaich made it a place of the Old Spirits in the Holy Age and it has never had walls, since the ancestors' ground was held to need none. It is a city of pilgrims and hostels, and the spirit-house keepers of Cnoc chiar and Inis bheag answer to its elders. Dubhan from the works below the town and books copied in its hostels are its trades; the elders have never blessed the works, since dubhan is not of the vein.

  • 20 am Faoilleach 2582 BDE — The ancestor-cairn at Cathair naomh
  • 19 an Lùnastal 1782 DE — Cathair naomh sends its wool
  • 5 an Giblean 1995 DE — Cathair naomh sends its rolls

Cnoc chiar

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,941

Founded 12 an Giblean 2403 BDE by spirit-house keepers of Cathair naomh. Known for way-shrines on the pilgrim road.

A dusky hill beside the harbour of Seann Toll, settled by keepers of the Old Spirits who tended waymarks on the pilgrim road to Cathair naomh. It remains a small town of hostels and way-shrines, busy in the feast seasons and empty between them.

Inis bheag

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,760

Founded 4 an Dàmhair 755 BDE by the island-keepers of Seann Toll. Known for the pilgrims' ferry to Cathair naomh.

A small walled harbour on a tidal islet of the north coast, near the holy city of Cathair naomh. It ferries pilgrims from the sea to the holy city and keeps the Old Spirits.

Seann Toll

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 19,261

Founded 8 an t-Samhain 12,898 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for sea-caves and the north-coast herring.

Seann Toll, old hollow, is named for the sea-caves under its headland, where Seann-Dhaoine marks are said to be cut into the rock. The Ròdaich resettled it in the Holy Age and it has been a fishing port ever since. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and the northern herring fleet.

Siorrachd Seann Vell

Cnoc chaol

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 5,467

Founded 23 am Faoilleach 128 DE by Ròdaich shore farmers of Seann Vell. Known for the town the Great Wave named.

Cnoc chaol is the town the Great Wave is named after. Tonn Mhòr Cnoc chaol struck the southern coast without warning in a single night, devastating it together with Cuan dhearg and Achadh mhin. The town was rebuilt higher up the narrow hill, and its people still leave the lowest street empty. Cnoc chaol and Cuan dhearg share Eilean bhàn, off the south coast.

  • 22 an Gearran 685 DE — Wave at Cnoc chaol
  • 23 an Dùbhlachd 1933 DE — Cnoc chaol rebuilt on the hill

Cuan chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,133

Founded 10 am Faoilleach 1192 DE by Ròdaich innkeepers of Seann Vell. Known for An Taigh-seinnse Mòr and steamed carp.

Cuan chrom is a river town on a bend of the Abhainn fhionn, and An Taigh-seinnse Mòr, one of the great houses of the old tavern circuit, stands at its river quay. The tavern was a waypoint on the mining roads and doubled as a militia halt in the years before the war. It is known across the island for its steamed carp and green brandy.

Cuan dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 14,659

Founded 31 am Faoilleach 1615 BDE by fishing clans of the southern shore. Known for rebuilt after the Great Wave.

A red-cliffed harbour on the southern coast that was a fishing town for three ages. The Great Wave, Tonn Mhòr Cnoc chaol, struck it in a single night in the first years of the new kingdom and destroyed the lower town with its fleet, and the harbour was rebuilt higher up the cliff. Its people keep the Old Spirits of the Ròdaich, and every house facing the sea keeps a lamp in the upper window. The harbour is on Eilean bhàn, the largest island off the south coast, which it shares with Cnoc chaol.

  • 5 am Màrt 480 DE — An Gàire Dubh
  • 23 an Giblean 1715 DE — Cuan dhearg flooded again
  • 24 an t-Samhain 1933 DE — The dead of the Great Wave counted
  • 9 an t-Iuchar 1956 DE — The harbour at Cuan dhearg reopened

Inis mhòr

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,975

Founded 12 an t-Sultain 691 DE by boatmen of Seann Vell. Known for barracks of the First Regiment.

An island town on the Abhainn fhionn, settled in the long quiet centuries by boatmen from Seann Vell upriver, Inis mhòr was walled once the capital's eastern approaches became worth defending. A' chiad rèisimeid, raised in the campaign of An Cogadh Fada, is stationed here and bears the town's name. Its barracks now outsize the old fishing quarter, and it lies within sight of the temple town of Cuan uaine, a little downriver; what it ships goes down the river to Cathair dhomhain. The white sand of its river banks goes to its glass-house.

  • 29 an Giblean 1929 DE — Coaling from Inis mhòr
  • 7 an Cèitean 2020 DE — A' chiad rèisimeid raised

Seann Vell

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,543

Founded 4 an t-Ògmhios 12,916 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for south-eastern citadel harbour.

Seann Vell of the south-east is a citadel harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site, resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. Its citadel guards the south-eastern coast and the approach to Seann Bhral, its larger neighbour and old rival. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. The town stands on Eilean dhearg, the island where the Seann-Dhaoine of the older Seann Vell laid their dead.

  • 8 am Faoilleach 11,197 BDE — The round houses of the eastern Seann Vell
  • 20 an Gearran 119 BDE — Seann Vell's harbour

Seann Vell

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,382

Founded 16 an Dàmhair 10,889 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for old harbour of the west coast.

Seann Vell of the west coast is a small harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site, the seat of its province. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age and took up the order of Manannan with the rest of the coast. An ceathramh cabhlach is stationed at Cuan shean, a short way up the coast. Its shire is the humans' old district of the outer coasts, kept whole: the islands of the west and south, Eilean bhàn with Cuan dhearg and Cnoc chaol, and the southern edge of the windy coast in the far north-west.

  • 20 an Giblean 10,480 BDE — The western Seann Vell
  • 4 an t-Samhain 150 BDE — Seann Vell swears on the sting
  • 20 an Giblean 1902 DE — The district of the outer coasts

Seann Vell

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 26,204

Founded 1 an t-Ògmhios 9251 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for walled river town on the Cuan chrom road.

Seann Vell of the capital's east is a walled river town on a Seann-Dhaoine site on the Abhainn fhionn and the seat of its province. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. An Taigh-seinnse Mòr stands just east of it, at the river quay of Cuan chrom.

  • 7 an t-Ògmhios 1839 DE — The flux reaches Seann Vell

Siorrachd Seann Warr

Seann Warr

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 19,842

Founded 27 am Màrt 11,799 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the Fifth Regiment's walled harbour.

Seann Warr is a Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the capital's western shore, resettled by the Ròdaich and walled in the Holy Age. Its citadel guards the western approaches to the capital. An còigeamh rèisimeid, raised in An Cogadh Fada, is stationed here and carries its name. Its salt-pans have sold salt since the first years of the humans' trade, and the flax of its lake-shore fields, pressed for linseed oil, is grown nowhere else on the island. Loch chrom is fresh, and the town's salt is boiled from brine springs that rise in the reed marsh behind it.

Siorrachd Tobar dhearg

Baile gharbh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,279

Founded 1 an t-Ògmhios 661 DE by the carters of Seann Vell. Known for an orthodox town of Brìde's flame on the coast road.

A rough town on the south coast road between Seann Vell and the lighthouse village of Tobar dhearg. It is one of the few towns where Òrd Bhrìde holds the majority, its orthodox druids having come from the pilgrim harbour at Caol naomh. It trades with Muileann naomh and the great port of Seann Skell.

Tobar dhearg

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 23,039

Founded 31 an Cèitean 110 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers of the southern coast. Known for the southern lighthouse and red well.

Tobar dhearg is a large village around a well of red water, the seat of its province. Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, one of the five lighthouses of the Age of Strangers, stands on the shore below it; it burned obsidian-lit flame for over a century before it was converted to dubhan. The village holds to Òrd Bhrìde, and its druids, keepers of Brìde's flame, keep the light's log.

  • 12 an Dàmhair 4654 BDE — Tobar dhearg on the southern cape
  • 28 am Màrt 407 DE — Fire at Tobar dhearg
  • 29 am Màrt 1795 DE — The first keeper of Tobar dhearg

Siorrachd Tobar fhiadhaich

Achadh gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 965

Founded 21 an Giblean 526 DE by Ròdaich peat-cutters of the northern uplands. Known for rough moor fields and peat.

A hamlet-sized village of rough moor fields and peat banks above Tobar fhiadhaich. Its peat warmed the northern towns when the Small-Burning Law still held and the ore was not burned freely. Fewer than a thousand people live there now.

Baile mhòr

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,585

Founded 17 an t-Iuchar 2873 BDE by herders of the northern moor. Known for moorland wool and an ill-fitting name.

The name promises a great town and the place has never been one; the chroniclers suppose it was large only beside the shielings around it when it was named. It is a quiet market for wool from the moor, dependent on Cnoc dhubh for its road and on Tobar fhiadhaich for its law. Its folk follow the druid schools of the Old Faith and keep a small reading-house where the druid schools' questions are argued on winter nights.

Cnoc dhubh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,435

Founded 22 an t-Sultain 1478 DE by the peat-cutters of the northern moor. Known for peat cut from the black hill.

A black hill of peat in the north, cut for fuel since the Small-Burning Law left the ore to the custodians and ordinary hearths to turf. It is the road-town for Baile mhòr and Àth shean and follows the druid schools of the Old Faith. The peat-banks are now nearly as worked out as the vein.

Cnoc ghlas

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 7,911

Founded 3 an Cèitean 403 BDE by hill shepherds of the northern coast. Known for grey slate and northern sheepwalks.

Cnoc ghlas is a hill town of the northern coast, a sheepwalk settlement of the Holy Age that later opened quarries in the grey slate of its hill. Its slate roofs much of the province of Tobar fhiadhaich. Its people follow the druid schools of the Old Faith, and the town sent more than its share of students to the schools' revival.

Muileann chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,206

Founded 27 an Gearran 432 DE by millers of Tobar fhiadhaich. Known for north-coast mill of Tobar fhiadhaich.

A mill town on the north coast, grinding for Tobar fhiadhaich and the upland farms behind it. It is one of several places named Muileann chrom and is not the great mill town of the central country. It is a quiet town of millers and inshore fishers.

Tobar fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 16,436

Founded 10 an t-Samhain 2045 BDE by Ròdaich herders of the northern moor. Known for wild spring and moorland grazing.

Tobar fhiadhaich is a large village around a wild spring on the moor, and the seat of its province. It lives on grazing and on the peat of Achadh gharbh. Its herders have walked the same moor paths since the Holy Age, and its spring is said never to have failed, even in the driest years.

  • 10 am Màrt 5711 BDE — Wolves at Tobar fhiadhaich
  • 18 an Giblean 1920 DE — The fever at Tobar fhiadhaich

Tobar ìseal

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,690

Founded 26 an Dùbhlachd 505 BDE by the well-keepers of Muileann shean. Known for the guarded low well.

A low well in a hollow below Muileann shean, ringed with stone in the Holy Age and watched ever since. The small keep that gives it a citadel was built to guard the water for the mill town in dry years, and the dry summers since have proved the builders right. It remains a village, owned in all but name by the millers upstream.

Siorrachd Tobar ghorm

Àth shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,697

Founded 15 an t-Iuchar 1340 BDE by the ford-lords of Tobar ghorm. Known for the old walled ford.

An old walled ford with a citadel in the north, holding the road between Tobar ghorm and Cnoc dhubh. Its keep was fought for in the war before the Severance. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Baile gheal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 7,515

Founded 2 an t-Ògmhios 1062 DE by the lime-burners of Tobar ghorm. Known for lime-kilns and whitewashed walls.

A white town named for the lime-kilns that whitened it, walled in the Age of Strangers after raids on the road to the harbour at Inis naomh. It is paired with Cnoc mhòr on the hill above, and the two share a market and a quarrel over which is older. Its people follow the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Inis naomh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,681

Founded 9 am Faoilleach 478 BDE by keepers of the holy isle. Known for holy isle and its walled landing.

Inis naomh is a walled harbour on a holy tidal isle of the north coast, reached on foot at low water, founded in the Holy Age. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith. Its walls were built to keep the isle's shrine safe from raiders.

Muileann mhin

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,313

Founded 8 an t-Iuchar 617 DE by millers of Tobar ghorm. Known for fine flour for Tobar ghorm.

Muileann mhin grinds the fine flour of Tobar ghorm, a short way east, and has risen and fallen with the larger village's harvests in every age. Its wheels are the oldest still turning in the province, and the miller families keep a roll of their masters going back to the Age of Sundering. In fair season the carts from the wool fairs come back loaded with its flour.

Tobar ghorm

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 25,305

Founded 31 am Faoilleach 2049 BDE by Ròdaich herders of the northern plain. Known for blue spring and wool fairs.

Tobar ghorm is a large village around a blue spring, the seat of its province, and home to the greatest wool fairs of the north. The fairs were old before the humans came, and the humans' wool-buyers made them larger. The mills of Muileann mhin grind its grain.

  • 25 an Giblean 1912 DE — A barracks at Tobar ghorm
